Crossfade</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Let your coding agent design in your open Figma file </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/crossfade?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1313559?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/crossfade" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9788"> <h2>#9788. Build an HTCondor Pool on Ubuntu and Run Your First Remote Job</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=1200,height=627,fit=cover,gravity=auto,format=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fgjp830vm9tr2klb01sb1.png" alt="Build an HTCondor Pool on Ubuntu and Run Your First Remote Job" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Part 1 of 6 in Building and Operating an HTCondor Pool for Research Computing.</p> <p>Suppose you have one training run per participant in a study and several workstations that could run them. With HTCondor, you can submit each run as a job and specify the CPU, memory, and GPU it needs. The workstations advertise what they can offer. HTCondor keeps each job in a queue until it can match it to a suitable machine. The machines that cooperate this way form a pool.</p> <p>I administer the central manager for our lab’s pool. Our November 2026 inventory lists twelve machines. The workstation that hosts the central manager also accepts submissions and runs jobs. Some of the other workstations only run jobs, while others also accept submissions.</p> <p>For this walkthrough, we’ll put each role on a separate Ubuntu 24.04 VM. You’ll submit a shell script and a text file from the access point (the submit node). The script will run on the worker and print its hostname and a line from the file. You’ll read both lines back on the access point.</p> <p>Start with three fresh VMs on a private network. Each needs Bash, curl, sudo, and access to the Ubuntu and HTCondor package repositories. Run uname -m on the access point and worker and check that the results match. The submit file below uses HTCondor’s default architecture requirement, which matches the architecture of the access point even when the executable is a shell script.</p> <p>Allow TCP port 9618 between pool members. Before installing, check name resolution on each host. Substitute your own hostnames below and confirm that each resolves to its intended private address.</p> <p>Start on the manager, then install the access point, then the worker. Enter the same pool password on all three. On each host, the installer uses that shared secret to generate a daemon token. The daemons use these tokens to authenticate to one another with HTCondor’s IDTOKENS method. Researchers submit jobs from their own local accounts on the access point.</p> <p>On each host, download the installer into your home directory. Set manager to the same real manager name everywhere. In a Bash shell on each host, first run the one assignment from its row, then run the common commands below. The installer takes the manager’s name even on the worker.</p> <p>The dry run shows the proposed installation commands. The 25.0 channel selects the HTCondor 25.0 LTS release series. Once the role and manager name look right, run the following in the same Bash session on that host. The silent prompt keeps the pool password out of your typed command history. The installer reads it from standard input.</p> <p>After the installer succeeds on each machine, check the installed version, the manager it points to, and the local service:</p> <p>Once the manager’s service is active, test its TCP port from both the access point and the worker. Use the manager variable you set on each host. On Ubuntu, nc is available in the netcat-openbsd package (sudo apt install netcat-openbsd if needed).</p> <p>If the connection times out or is refused, check the manager’s service, the resolved address, and the firewall rules. A successful connection establishes TCP reachability. To check whether the daemons have also registered with the collector, run the following on the access point after all three services have started. Allow time for their first advertisements.</p> <p>For this layout, look for all three hosts in the first query, the access point in the second, and at least one slot on the worker in the third. A master entry tells you that the host’s managing daemon advertised itself. The slot entry tells you what that worker is offering. A machine can appear in the first list while offering no slots.</p> <p>Log in to the access point as a regular user. Create a working directory. Put a short script and a text file in it:</p> <p>In that directory, save this as first.sub. HTCondor will transfer the executable and the specified input file, so the worker can run the test without a shared home directory, NAS mount, or Python environment.</p> <p>Submit the job and note the cluster number printed by condor_submit. A quick job may already have finished by the time you inspect the queue.</p> <p>Set cluster to the number printed at submission. The submit file queues one process, so its job ID ends in .0. Wait up to three minutes for a completion or removal event.</p> <p>If the wait times out or reports an error, use the troubleshooting steps below. A zero exit status from condor_wait can also mean the job was removed. Check the job’s own exit status and read its standard output on the access point.</p> <p>For a successful run, expect 4 false 0 in the history. These values mean the job completed, exited normally, and returned exit code zero. The output file should look like this.</p> <p>The first line should match the output of hostname on your worker. The second shows that the script read the transferred file. Reading both lines on the access point confirms that stdout made the return trip.</p> <p>If the wait times out, the job may still be queued or running. On the access point, check its state and recent events.</p> <p>JobStatus 1 means Idle, 2 means Running, and 5 means Held. For a running job, repeat the wait with the same ID. If the queue query returns no row, check the history again. If the event log is missing, check the cluster number and make sure you are in ~/first-condor-job.</p> <p>For workstations joining our existing lab pool, I issue the daemon token centrally. A colleague sends me the workstation’s network address. I create the token on the central manager with condor_token_create and give it to the colleague. They configure the workstation with our manager and trust domain and install the token under /etc/condor/tokens.d/ with restricted permissions.</p> <p>Our central manager is configured with use ROLE : CentralManager, Submit, Execute. For a workstation that will both accept submissions and run jobs, our setup instructions specify use ROLE : Submit, Execute. I look for its schedd with condor_status -schedd and its execution slots with condor_status. Submitting a job from the colleague’s local account checks that the workstation’s schedd accepts jobs from that user. To see which workstation actually ran the job, check the hostname printed by the probe.</p> <p>People also use these workstations at their desks. Our setup instructions use START = (Cpus > 0) && (LoadAvg / Cpus < 0.4) to decide when a slot can accept a new job. A workstation can remain visible in the pool while this condition prevents a new job from starting. On a partitionable slot, Cpus counts the CPUs still available. As jobs claim CPUs, the denominator gets smaller, so even an unchanged LoadAvg can bring the ratio up to the cutoff.</p> <p>After the CPU test succeeds, you can configure HTCondor to let two jobs share one NVIDIA GPU. On the idle worker, check that nvidia-smi -L lists the expected card, then apply the settings below.</p> <p>-divide 2 makes condor_gpu_discovery list the same device ID twice in DetectedGPUs and report half its usual GlobalMemoryMb value for matching. Two jobs that each request one GPU can therefore be assigned the same card. They share its VRAM, and either job can use more than the advertised half if enough memory is free. Once the worker advertises again, run condor_status -gpus on the access point to inspect the pool’s GPU resources.</p> <p>AI assistance was used in drafting and editing this article.</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/nha6ki/build-an-htcondor-pool-on-ubuntu-and-run-your-first-remote-job-58b7" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9787"> <h2>#9787. Top 10 AI Tools in 2023 That Will Make Your Life Easier</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><br /></span></p><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiu91xnR3LQV62WoiA0scuFOTa-Xx9vIwouaceeyosFtZrJB0UivYIWtbcF3TCWEjKhRQVBiSeB00RQI0-cO_eBG6d05_6UV7zYw9qzyHMJ6u2m9_itNW2mFAS8LChEhhJQ14aJbI3GrkEsY9xCTExAT-qxUSh5asVFMAmX-ceWufpgV_DrG9tk3Y4umw/s1920/Blue%20Purple%20Futuristic%20Modern%203D%20Tech%20Company%20Business%20Presentation-min.jpg" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><img alt="top 10 ai tools in 2023 that will make your life easier" border="0" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiu91xnR3LQV62WoiA0scuFOTa-Xx9vIwouaceeyosFtZrJB0UivYIWtbcF3TCWEjKhRQVBiSeB00RQI0-cO_eBG6d05_6UV7zYw9qzyHMJ6u2m9_itNW2mFAS8LChEhhJQ14aJbI3GrkEsY9xCTExAT-qxUSh5asVFMAmX-ceWufpgV_DrG9tk3Y4umw/w640-h360/Blue%20Purple%20Futuristic%20Modern%203D%20Tech%20Company%20Business%20Presentation-min.jpg" title="top 10 ai tools in 2023 that will make your life easier" width="640" /></span></a></div><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><br /></span><p><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"> In this article, we explore the top 10 AI tools that are driving innovation and efficiency in various industries. These tools are designed to automate repetitive tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity. The tools included in our list are some of the most advanced and widely used in the market, and are suitable for a variety of applications. Some of the tools focus on natural language processing, such as ChatGPT and Grammarly, while others focus on image and video generation, such as DALL-E and Lumen5. Other tools such as OpenAI Codex, Tabnine, Canva, Jasper AI,, and Surfer SEO are designed to help with specific tasks such as code understanding content writing and website optimization. This list is a great starting point for anyone looking to explore the possibilities of AI and how it can be applied to their business or project.</span></p><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">So let’s dive into</span></p> <h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">1. ChatGPT</span></h3> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">ChatGPT is a large language model that generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts. It can be used for tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion. It can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing, and generates coherent and fluent text, but should be used with care as it may generate text that is biased, offensive, or factually incorrect.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><b>Pros:</b></span></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can generate coherent and fluent text, even when completing a given text prompt.</span></li> </ul> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><b>Cons:</b></span></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">May generate text that is biased or offensive</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can generate text that is not accurate or factually correct</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">May require large amounts of computational resources to run</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The model can sometimes generate text that is not coherent or fluent, depending on the prompt given.</span></li> </ul> <span style="font-family: Montserrat;"> <div id="atContainer-504b591a28719b1270e09aa4045e24ab"></div> </span><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Overall, ChatGPT is a powerful tool for natural language processing, but it should be used with care and with an understanding of its limitations.</span></p> <h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">2. DALL-E</span></h3><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">DALL-E is a generative model developed by OpenAI that is capable of generating images from text prompts. It is based on the GPT-3 architecture, which is a transformer-based neural network language model that has been trained on a massive dataset of text. DALL-E can generate images that are similar to a training dataset and it can generate high-resolution images that are suitable for commercial use.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><b>Pros:</b></span></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Generates high-resolution images</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can generate images from text prompts</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">It can be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as generating images of a certain style or category</span></li> </ul> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><b>Cons:</b></span></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">May generate images that are not entirely original and could be influenced by the training data</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">May require significant computational resources to run</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The quality of the generated images may vary depending on the specific prompt</span></li> </ul> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Overall, DALL-E is a powerful AI-based tool for generating images, it can be used for a variety of applications such as creating images for commercial use, gaming, and other creative projects. It is important to note that the generated images should be reviewed and used with care, as they may not be entirely original and could be influenced by the training data.</span></p> <h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">3. Lumen5</span></h3><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Lumen5 is a content creation platform that uses AI to help users create videos, social media posts, and other types of content. It has several features that make it useful for content creation and marketing, including:</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Pros:</span></b></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Automatically summarizes text from a blog post, article, or another source into a script for a video or social media post</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Offers a library of royalty-free videos, images, and music to use in content</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Has a drag-and-drop interface for easy content creation</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can create videos in multiple languages</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Has a built-in analytics tool to track the performance of created content.</span></li> </ul> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><b>Cons:</b></span></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The automatic summarization feature may not always capture the main points of the source material</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The library of videos, images, and music is limited.</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The analytics feature is basic</span></li> </ul> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Overall, Lumen5 is a useful tool for creating content quickly and easily, it can help automate the process of creating videos, social media posts, and other types of content. However, the quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material and it is important to review and edit the content before publishing it.</span></p> <h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">4. Grammarly</span></h3><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Grammarly is a writing-enhancement platform that uses AI to check for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text. It also provides suggestions for improving the clarity, concision, and readability of the text. It has several features that make it useful for improving writing, including:</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Pros:</span></b></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Checks for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Provides suggestions for improving clarity, concision, and readability</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can be integrated with various apps and platforms such as Microsoft Office, Google Docs, and social media platforms</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Offers a browser extension and a desktop app</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Has a premium version with more advanced features such as plagiarism detection and more</span></li> </ul> <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Cons:</span></b></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The suggestions provided may not always be accurate or appropriate</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The grammar checker may not always recognize context-specific language use</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The free version has limited features</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Limited to English language only</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Overall, Grammarly is a useful tool for improving writing, it can help users identify and correct grammar and punctuation errors, and improve the clarity, concision, and readability of their text. However, it is important to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate.</span></li> </ul> <h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">5.OpenAI Codex</span></h3><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">OpenAI Codex is a system developed by OpenAI that can create code from natural language descriptions of software tasks. The system is based on the GPT-3 model and can generate code in multiple programming languages.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;"><b>Pros:</b></span></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can automate the process of writing code</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can help developers to be more productive</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can help non-technical people to create software</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Can generate code in multiple programming languages</span></li> </ul> <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Cons:</span></b></p> <ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The generated code may not always be optimal or efficient</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">The system may not be able to handle complex software tasks</span></li> <li class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the code.</span></li> </ul> <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-family: Montserrat;">Overall, OpenAI Codex is a powerful tool that can help automate the process of writing code and make it more accessible to non-technical people. However, the quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description and it is important to review and test the code before using it in a production environment. Measuring Offline-First Sync Performance on Mobile</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=1200,height=627,fit=cover,gravity=auto,format=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fxrxvrrwrlpyszlrwxgkk.supabase.co%2Fstorage%2Fv1%2Fobject%2Fpublic%2Fproject-images%2Fblog%2Foffline-first-sync-on-mobile-measuring-before-optimising.jpg" alt="Measuring Offline-First Sync Performance on Mobile" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Posted on Nov 13 • Originally published at amitchakraborty.dev</p> <p>Say you are a mobile developer tasked with optimizing the offline-first sync functionality of your React Native application. Your users are complaining about slow sync times, and you suspect that the current implementation is not efficient. However, before embarking on a potentially costly rewrite, you want to understand the current performance characteristics of your sync mechanism. You've tried using the application on a slow network, but it's difficult to quantify the issues and prioritize optimizations.</p> <p>Offline-first sync is a complex problem, involving caching, conflict resolution, and network communication. On mobile devices, additional constraints such as limited storage, processing power, and network bandwidth come into play. Without proper instrumentation, it's challenging to identify the bottlenecks in the sync pipeline. The symptoms of poor performance can be misleading, and optimizing the wrong components can lead to wasted effort and even introduce new issues.</p> <p>To measure the performance of your offline-first sync, follow these steps:</p> <p>Instrumenting your sync pipeline and collecting performance data will incur some overhead in terms of development time and resources. However, this investment is crucial to ensure that any optimization efforts are targeted and effective. If your application's sync performance is not a major concern, or if you have limited resources, you may need to prioritize other features or bug fixes. Additionally, if your application's sync mechanism is relatively simple, the benefits of instrumentation may not outweigh the costs.</p> <p>When interviewing a candidate for a mobile development position, you may ask a question like: "How would you approach optimizing the offline-first sync performance of a React Native application?" A weak answer might focus on general optimization techniques without considering the specific challenges of offline-first sync. A strong answer would discuss the importance of instrumentation, the need to understand the performance characteristics of the sync mechanism, and the potential trade-offs involved in optimization efforts. For example:</p> <p>Amit Chakraborty is a founding engineer and senior architect — React Native, AI/RAG systems and production architecture. Portfolio: www.amitchakraborty.dev · LinkedIn · GitHub. CI Failure Triage Needs Evidence Before It Needs a Classifier</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/g1WeGoqPdQfjArop5JSl3omfg7J3-4083g11.jpeg" alt="CI Failure Triage Needs Evidence Before It Needs a Classifier" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>If you have ever owned a CI pipeline and cleared a wall of red builds before standup, you might recognize this routine. A nightly run finishes with thirty-seven failed tests, and by the time anyone looks, thirty have passed on a rerun and picked up a flaky tag while the other seven get tickets.</p> <p>Nobody records why the thirty failed in the first place, so the same failures come back the next night under the same label. And it is easy to see why teams settle into this, because a rerun clears the build in minutes while finding the real cause of thirty failures could take the whole team a day.</p> <p>That gap is where a new class of AI models starts to look tempting. Shawn Gordon’s recent HackerNoon explainer introduces Jev, a decision model from TypeSafe AI that writes nothing and only picks an answer. It chooses from up to 255 options or returns a yes or no probability in about half a second. TypeSafe also says those probabilities are calibrated, so an answer given at 80 percent confidence should be right about 80 percent of the time.</p> <p>Sorting a failed test into a product defect, environment noise, or an agent error is a three-option choice question, which makes it look like a natural fit. But when Mastra, the company behind an open-source framework for building AI agents in TypeScript, tested Jev on a related triage job, the results were poor.</p> <p>Jev labeled 78 of Mastra’s own GitHub issues as urgent, high, or low, using only each issue’s title and body, and only about 10 of its answers matched an engineer’s judgment. Mastra concluded that the model could not see the evidence that priority depends on, and Gordon put the risk plainly in his explainer. “A consistently wrong classifier that runs cheaply is just a faster way to tag things badly.”</p> <p>CI triage has the same trap, because a model can sort failures well only when the pipeline has kept the evidence that separates one category from another. So the evidence has to come first and the classifier second.</p> <p>Most pipelines record a failed test as one status, and that single status hides three kinds of failure that need different fixes from different teams.</p> <p>Sai Krishna, Director of Engineering at TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest), draws that line before any fix starts. “We should ideally treat these failures into three different categories,” he explains. “Whether it is a product defect, like an actual defect in the product. Or if it is environmental noise, maybe a network issue, a latency problem, a backend API that went down. Or very importantly now, since agentic pipelines are involved, whether it is an agent error.”</p> <p>He also gives a working definition for the third category, which is the one teams find hardest to name. “If the agent’s reasoning or actions are inconsistent, that is the point where we can clearly say it is an agent error,” Krishna says. “We have to put them in different buckets.”</p> <p>Each bucket leaves a different trail, and that trail is what a classifier will eventually read. A product defect reproduces on the same commit under the same conditions and usually traces back to a recent change in the application. Environment noise shows up as timeouts or 5xx responses from a dependency, and it tends to hit unrelated tests in the same time window.</p> <p>An agent error happens in a healthy environment and with an unchanged commit, while the agent’s steps differ from the last passing run. So the first practical move is to write those signals down as rules for each bucket and to name an owner for each one. The feature team takes defects, the platform team takes noise, and whoever owns the prompt and the model takes agent errors.</p> <p>Three buckets cover most failures, but some failures look like environment noise only because of how the suite runs.</p> <p>Srinivasan Sekar, also Director of Engineering at TestMu AI, sees this most often when teams move from local runs to large parallel grids. “The most common and unanticipated failure is shared state across parallel workers,” he highlights. “Locally, one or two tests run in parallel, and everything works, but in the cloud with 200 parallel workers you suddenly see tests depending on specific execution order.” The usual causes are global fixtures or singletons that several tests change at once, race conditions in test data setup, and ordering dependencies that nobody noticed while the suite ran one test at a time.</p> <p>These failures are test defects. And a classifier that only knows three labels will file them as environment noise, because they come and go without any change to the code. The fix is to add a fourth label and give the classifier the one signal that separates it, which is whether the test still fails with a single worker.</p> <p>Rerunning each failure once with one worker inside the triage job costs a few seconds and turns an ambiguous failure into a clear one. And the repair itself belongs in the test, through per-worker test data and idempotent setup and teardown, and not in the infrastructure.</p> <p>Agent errors are the hardest bucket to fill correctly, because the evidence is in decisions the agent made and not in any log the pipeline already keeps.</p> <p>Tom Howe, Director of Insight Engineering, built his team’s approach around those decisions. His team captures a trace of every action an agent takes, with full context, in a cryptographically secure audit system. It then uses separate agent evaluators to review those traces for logic errors that have happened or might happen next.</p> <p>“The steps that the non-deterministic system takes to get to an output are as important to test as the outputs themselves,” he explains. “By examining a detailed trace of the steps an agent takes and the tools it leverages to generate an output, you can get deep insight into where decisions are brittle and anticipate errors before they happen.”</p> <p>That trace is also the missing input for automated triage. After its test, Mastra advised letting an agent gather the evidence first and letting the classifier judge what it gathered, and CI works the same way. A triage job can attach an evidence bundle to every failure before any model sees it.</p> <p>The bundle carries the commit, the model and prompt versions, dependency health at the start of the run, the retry outcome, and a diff of the agent’s steps against the last passing run.</p> <p>Every field in that bundle points at a bucket. A degraded payments API points at noise, a failure with eight workers followed by a pass with one points at a test defect, and a changed step sequence on a healthy environment points at an agent error. When the signals conflict, as they do in this example, the bundle shows the conflict instead of hiding it. A person reading this bundle can usually name the bucket quickly, and so can a decision model.</p> <p>Once the evidence exists, the classifier’s job is narrow, and keeping it narrow is what makes it safe to automate.</p> <p>Shahram Anver, Co-Founder and CEO of Cleric, which builds AI SRE agents for incident investigation, shows how far that labeling can go once a team has the evidence to support it. His team tracks 51 failure mode labels across its agent investigations. Those labels separate tool access problems from reasoning errors, omitted steps, and unfinished runs, because a status that only says the agent responded tells the team nothing about whether it did useful work.</p> <p>Most CI teams do not need 51 labels on day one, but Anver’s taxonomy shows that the label set should grow as the evidence gets richer. A decision model makes that growth cheap, because a choice question over four labels or forty costs about the same to run. The harder design question is the rule for acting on each answer. The code below sends a failure straight to its owner only when the model is confident, and puts everything else in a human triage queue.</p> <p>The threshold should come from the team’s own data and not from a vendor’s claim. Public write-ups on Jev note that most claims about the model come from TypeSafe itself and that no calibration results have been published yet. So run the classifier in shadow mode for two weeks, keep human labels for the same failures, and check whether answers given at 90 percent confidence are actually right about 90 percent of the time.</p> <p>If the 0.9 bucket comes back at 0.70 accuracy, the model is overconfident on this team’s failures. In that case, raise the threshold or improve the bundle before letting it route anything on its own.</p> <p>Krishna treats the classifier as the last step of triage, not the first. “A model can sort failures faster than anyone on the team, but only if the pipeline kept what that model needs to see,” he says. “Start by labeling a month of failures by hand. Once your own engineers agree on the buckets, a classifier has something real to learn from and something real to be checked against.”</p> <p>The first week of this work needs no model at all. Pull the last month of failed and flaky tests, label each one by hand as a product defect, environment noise, an agent error, or a test defect, and note which piece of evidence decided the label. Then make the triage job attach those pieces of evidence to every new failure, run a decision model in shadow mode against the hand labels, and switch on automatic routing only for the labels where its confidence matches its accuracy.</p> <p>SWE-bench Scores Say Nothing About the Code Your Reviewers Inherit</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://hackernoon.com/ci-failure-triage-needs-evidence-before-it-needs-a-classifier?source=rss" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9781"> <h2>#9781. Building a Sticky Mobile Call Bar for a Law Firm Website</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=1200,height=627,fit=cover,gravity=auto,format=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fowptpm8ucvak6m4rhaqd.png" alt="Building a Sticky Mobile Call Bar for a Law Firm Website" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Most visitors to a criminal defense website arrive on a phone, and many of them want to call rather than read. A sticky call bar, a strip pinned to the bottom of the screen with a tap-to-call button, is one of the most common patterns on law firm sites for that reason. It is also one of the most commonly broken. Bars cover footer links, collide with chat widgets, sit under the iPhone home indicator or hide the last line of every page.</p> <p>This post walks through building one that behaves well: correct on notched phones, accessible, easy to measure and out of the way of the content. The examples use plain HTML and CSS with a few lines of JavaScript, so they port to any CMS or framework.</p> <p>Keep the bar simple. One primary action, the phone call, and at most one secondary action, such as a link to the contact form. Two buttons fit comfortably on small screens. Three usually do not.</p> <p>Use a real tel: link with the number in international format, and put the human-readable number in the visible text. Screen reader users and people who distrust buttons both benefit from seeing the actual number. Wrap the bar in a landmark element with a label so assistive technology can identify it.</p> <p>On phones with a home indicator, content at the very bottom of the viewport can sit underneath it. CSS environment variables solve this, but only if the viewport meta tag opts in with viewport-fit=cover. Without that, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) returns zero and the bar may be partly covered.</p> <p>The body padding matters. Without it, the bar covers the last part of every page, which on a law firm site is often the footer with the disclaimer and office addresses. Match the padding to the bar's real height, and test with large text settings, since the bar grows when the user increases the font size.</p> <p>WCAG 2.2 added a target size criterion at level AA that sets a minimum of 24 by 24 CSS pixels for most targets, with some exceptions. That is a floor. For the main call button on a defense site, aim much larger, around 44 to 48 pixels tall, since the person tapping it may be stressed, in a car or using one hand.</p> <p>Check contrast too. A white phone number on a pale brand color may look fine in a design file and fail outdoors on a phone. Run the colors through a contrast checker and aim for at least the AA ratio for normal text.</p> <p>Decide on a stacking order and stick to it. Common choices are to move the chat launcher above the bar with a bottom offset, or to fold chat into the bar as the secondary action. Hide the bar while the on-screen keyboard is open on form pages, since it can cover the field the user is typing in. Listening for focus on inputs and toggling a class works on most devices.</p> <p>A call bar on every page is the default, but it is worth reconsidering. On a long charge page, the bar keeps the number in reach. On the contact page, which already shows the number and a form, it adds clutter. On a printable page, such as courthouse directions, hide it in a print stylesheet.</p> <p>Some sites reveal the bar only after the visitor scrolls past the first screen, so the hero section stays clean. That can work, but test it. A visitor who wants to call immediately should not have to scroll to find the number.</p> <p>Content matters as much as code. The words on the button affect whether people tap it, and plain labels such as "Call now" next to the actual number tend to be clearer than vague promises. This article on writing the words around the call button on a defense site covers the copy side.</p> <p>Track taps on the call link as an event in your analytics tool. Attach the listener to the link and do not prevent the default action, so the dialer still opens if the analytics script is slow or blocked. Record which page the tap came from, since that is the data the marketing side will ask for.</p> <p>Remember that a tap is not a call. Some users tap and hang up before connecting. If the firm uses a call tracking service, compare tap events with connected calls by page every month to see how far the numbers drift apart.</p> <p>Emulators catch layout problems, but they miss the details that matter here: the home indicator, the dynamic toolbar in mobile browsers that changes the viewport height while scrolling, and how the bar behaves when the keyboard opens. Test on at least one recent iPhone and one Android phone, held upright and turned sideways, with the system font size turned up.</p> <p>For more on design for defense firm websites, the law firm website design guides cover layout, typography and mobile patterns.</p> <p>A small bar that does not cover the main content is generally fine. Avoid anything that hides most of the screen on page load, since intrusive overlays can create a poor experience on mobile.</p> <p>Usually not. Desktop visitors rarely place calls from the browser, and a header with the phone number serves them better.</p> <p>Yes, with an sms: link, if the firm actually monitors that number. Make sure someone replies quickly and that texting fits the firm's intake rules.</p> <p>SBD Marketing works only with criminal defense firms, one per city. It designs and builds websites for defense practices, handles SEO for the charges they defend, runs SEO audits and works on visibility in AI search tools.</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/sbdmarketing/building-a-sticky-mobile-call-bar-for-a-law-firm-website-1569" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9780"> <h2>#9780. How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2023-10/Soften-Butter_1837.jpg" alt="How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions.</p> <p>Ryan from our Baker’s Hotline is here with the answer.</p> <p>You sure can! It will still work the next time you want to bake. But remember, as with any dairy product, there are always precautions to take.</p> <p>The USDA recommends keeping butter at room temperature for no more than two days to prevent spoilage. Salt is a preservative and can lengthen the shelf life, but for the sake of this article, we’re talking about unsalted butter. (It’s more appropriate for baking and is the type called for in most King Arthur recipes.)</p> <p>“If the butter has only been on the counter at room temperature for a few hours or overnight and has maintained a temperature below 70°F, it should be just fine to place back in the fridge,” says Ryan. “You may not notice a difference in the performance of the butter when you eventually use it, other than the wrapper being a bit wet or soft. Food safety-wise, it’s still good to use.”</p> <p>“If the butter became very soft or started to melt during its time on the counter (or in the microwave if you were speeding up the process), you can put it back in the fridge, but it may not be the best to use in your recipe,” Ryan suggests. “You may notice when it solidifies that it’s separated or grainy. The water, fats, and solids in butter are an emulsion, which can break when melted and re-solidified.” If your recipe depends on butter to create air or structure, like a cake that calls for creaming butter and sugar, you’ll want to start over with new butter.</p> <p>“If you used that butter in a recipe requiring creaming, the air you incorporate wouldn’t be as stable since the structure of the butter has changed,” Ryan says. “Your baked goods may not rise properly, and frostings may be soft and loose. Is it still safe to use? Food safety-wise, yes. But structure-wise, perhaps not.”</p> <p>That butter can still be used for other things though! Extra-softened or even melted and re-solidified butter will still work perfectly to spread on toast or pancakes, to be made into brown butter, or to remelt and use in recipes calling for melted butter like a Graham Cracker Crust.</p> <p>If your butter has been unrefrigerated for more than two days, you run the risk of it going rancid. As Ryan says, “There is no coming back from rancid butter.” It has a distinctly unpleasant flavor and a noticeable rancid smell that carries over into baked goods. It’s best to dispose of the butter if this happens.</p> <p>But what if you want to keep your butter at room temperature for days at a time to slather on your morning toast? Ryan recommends storing your butter in a butter keeper if you want to leave it on the counter. “The water in the base of the jar creates an airtight seal, helping prevent the butter from spoiling. So long as it is stored away from direct heat and light, the butter in a container like this will be fine for a few days. Be sure to replace the water often and clean the container before filling again.”</p> <p>“When working with butter in a recipe, I like to bring out and soften only the amount that is needed for what I am working on. That way, I don’t end up with extra butter that won’t be used right away,” he says. “Repeatedly moving butter from the fridge to the counter and then back invites spoilage and poor performance.”</p> <p>In a rush? To soften your butter more quickly, Ryan advises, “Cut your butter into pats and place them on a plate in a single layer at room temperature. More surface area means that the butter will soften a bit faster!”</p> <p>Photography by Rick Holbrook; food styling by Kaitlin Wayne.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Because we're all wondering what to do with our apple and pumpkin pies.</p> <p>It can be trickier than you think — here’s what to look for.</p> <p>Here’s how to make scones moist, every time.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/01/how-long-can-butter-sit-out" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9779"> <h2>#9779. Sendr V4: Lovable for GTM</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Your AI GTM engineer to build signal based go-to-market </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/sendr?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1267000?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/sendr" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9778"> <h2>#9778. Omnigraph</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Open source graph database for your AI agents </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/omnigraph?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1298575?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/omnigraph" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9777"> <h2>#9777. LimeWire AI Studio Review 2023: Details, Pricing & Features</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"> </span></p><p style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">In the rapidly advancing landscape of AI technology and innovation, LimeWire emerges as a unique platform in the realm of generative AI tools. This platform not only stands out from the multitude of existing AI tools but also brings a fresh approach to content generation. LimeWire not only empowers users to create AI content but also provides creators with creative ways to share and monetize their creations.</span></p><p style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">As we explore LimeWire, our aim is to uncover its features, benefits for creators, and the exciting possibilities it offers for AI content generation. This platform presents an opportunity for users to harness the power of AI in image creation, all while enjoying the advantages of a free and accessible service.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">Let's unravel the distinctive features that set LimeWire apart in the dynamic landscape of AI-powered tools, understanding how creators can leverage its capabilities to craft unique and engaging AI-generated images.</span></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></h2><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">Introduction</span></h2><div><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgjpMlV4umM2-ZY3vAwynTzCWwbk5_pjVyGQqGGftHzeOmpTyc4aYApxfanU29DyPfjUZz5ZhhDojKe8mpYUG6tcEezDQrg1NTDr8XOBequWD3LOpUKpea4AiaB5mhPpYZSxtk2lRfHnCSNhyphenhyphenXm53l80cTMNA_KtCMfDd9PQNzYWp6A4ylQJtUy_-7GpWsF/s1100/limewire-studio.jpg" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><img alt="limewire" border="0" height="354" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgjpMlV4umM2-ZY3vAwynTzCWwbk5_pjVyGQqGGftHzeOmpTyc4aYApxfanU29DyPfjUZz5ZhhDojKe8mpYUG6tcEezDQrg1NTDr8XOBequWD3LOpUKpea4AiaB5mhPpYZSxtk2lRfHnCSNhyphenhyphenXm53l80cTMNA_KtCMfDd9PQNzYWp6A4ylQJtUy_-7GpWsF/w640-h354/limewire-studio.jpg" title="limewire" width="640" /></span></a></div><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><div><span><br /></span></div>LimeWire, a name once associated with the notorious file-sharing tool from the 2000s, has undergone a significant transformation. The LimeWire we discuss today is not the file-sharing application of the past but has re-emerged as an entirely new entity—a cutting-edge AI content publishing platform.</span></div><div><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></div><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">This revamped LimeWire invites users to register and unleash their creativity by crafting original AI content, which can then be shared and showcased on the LimeWire Studio. Notably, even acclaimed artists and musicians, such as Deadmau5, Soulja Boy, and Sean Kingston, have embraced this platform to publish their content in the form of NFT music, videos, and images.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">Beyond providing a space for content creation and sharing, LimeWire introduces monetization models to empower users to earn revenue from their creations. This includes avenues such as earning ad revenue and participating in the burgeoning market of Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs). As we delve further, we'll explore these monetization strategies in more detail to provide a comprehensive understanding of LimeWire's innovative approach to content creation and distribution.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">LimeWire Studio welcomes content creators into its fold, providing a space to craft personalized AI-focused content for sharing with fans and followers. Within this creative hub, every piece of content generated becomes not just a creation but a unique asset—ownable and tradable. Fans have the opportunity to subscribe to creators' pages, immersing themselves in the creative journey and gaining ownership of digital collectibles that hold tradeable value within the LimeWire community. Notably, creators earn a 2.5% royalty each time their content is traded, adding a rewarding element to the creative process.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">The platform's flexibility is evident in its content publication options. Creators can choose to share their work freely with the public or opt for a premium subscription model, granting exclusive access to specialized content for subscribers.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><a href="https://limewire.com/studio?referrer=fll3a5fl9p" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">LimeWire AI Studio</a></span></h2><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">As of the present moment, LimeWire focuses on AI Image Generation, offering a spectrum of creative possibilities to its user base. This strategic expansion promises creators even more avenues for expression and engagement with their audience, positioning LimeWire Studio as a dynamic and evolving platform within the realm of AI-powered content creation.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">AI Image Generation Tools</span></h2><div><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgDTFvirsSedRuEhryeV3Thmn7FWknlYW0Dsem9LJqFfty8EotENaiCNW1LKX4eDMzca19saIgLBIi9p5mh_qzeKz_JD5kqtgOhPXfRyQkPzT5Jc_QlUcAqTFPlV_6s7EBgmezCHUzosiDtmpoQDUK8fw9wYQyYsFBea3ahvFlDrx25ApnOuvZ0z7shxGJQ/s1100/ss.jpg" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><img alt="limewire AI Studio" border="0" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgDTFvirsSedRuEhryeV3Thmn7FWknlYW0Dsem9LJqFfty8EotENaiCNW1LKX4eDMzca19saIgLBIi9p5mh_qzeKz_JD5kqtgOhPXfRyQkPzT5Jc_QlUcAqTFPlV_6s7EBgmezCHUzosiDtmpoQDUK8fw9wYQyYsFBea3ahvFlDrx25ApnOuvZ0z7shxGJQ/w640-h360/ss.jpg" title="limewire-studio" width="640" /></span></a></div><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /><span><br /></span></span></div><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">The <a href="https://limewire.com/studio?referrer=fll3a5fl9p" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">LimeWire AI image generation</a> tool presents a versatile platform for both the creation and editing of images. You can experiment with the AI image and content generation tools and share your creations while earning a small income on the side.</span></p><p><br /></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">LMWR Tokens</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">The revenue you earn from your creations will come in the form of LMWR tokens, LimeWire’s own cryptocurrency.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">Your earnings will be paid every month in LMWR, which you can then trade on many popular crypto exchange platforms like Kraken, ByBit, and UniSwap.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">You can also use your LMWR tokens to pay for prompts when using LimeWire generative AI tools.</span></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">Pricing Plans</span></h2><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">You can sign up to LimeWire to use its AI tools for free. Oxygen;">In conclusion, LimeWire emerges as a democratizing force in the creative landscape, providing an inclusive platform where anyone can unleash their artistic potential and effortlessly share their work. With the integration of AI, LimeWire eliminates traditional barriers, empowering designers, musicians, and artists to publish their creations and earn revenue with just a few clicks.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Oxygen;">The ongoing commitment of LimeWire to innovation is evident in its plans to enhance generative AI tools with new features and models.
