As LimeWire continues to evolve, creators are encouraged to stay tuned for the launch of its forthcoming AI music and video generation tools, promising a future brimming with creative potential and endless artistic exploration</span></p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://techncruncher.blogspot.com/2023/12/limewire-ai-studio-review-2023-details.html" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9776"> <h2>#9776. I Put a 42-Desk Design Studio Inside My Coding Agent</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/nm8nG98qHqTz1QInSYwdBWsK07k1-4o83b5v.png" alt="I Put a 42-Desk Design Studio Inside My Coding Agent" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>I work on slow clicks and missing browser traces. I'm an OpenTelemetry Browser approver.</p> <p>I work on slow clicks and missing browser traces. I'm an OpenTelemetry Browser approver.</p> <p>I work on slow clicks and missing browser traces. I'm an OpenTelemetry Browser approver.</p> <p>In October, I pointed Desk Studio at its own launch card. Three roughs, one pick, three polish rounds, scored 8.4, then 8.5, then 8.9, signed off at 8.9 for $1.34 at list price. And I could see every one of those steps while it happened, which is the whole reason the tool exists.</p> <p>Before it, a follow-up like "make the headline bigger" would come back from my coding agent as a whole new design. New layout, new colors, sometimes new copy. Was the headline fixed? Couldn't tell, cause everything else moved too.</p> <p>So Desk Studio splits the job up like a small studio. Rough options first, then one gets picked with notes, a cheaper desk polishes it, a script checks the real pixels, and a senior desk signs it off or sends it back. I still use it on my own projects.</p> <p>There are 42 desks. The Design Manager runs in your own session and hands out work. The other 41 run as subagents, things like a Typographer, an Art Director, a UI Designer, or an Email Designer. Each one is just a markdown brief in the repo, so if you want to know how the Art Director decides, you open agents/art-director.md and read it.</p> <p>They're grouped into three tiers, and each tier is on a model that suits what it does.</p> <p>It all runs locally. The desks reach models through whatever CLI you're already logged into, claude, codex or agy, or an API key if you'd rather. Apart from those model calls and a few web lookups from the research desks, nothing leaves your machine.</p> <p>In Claude Code it's a plugin. For Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Windsurf or OpenCode it's one line in the project:</p> <p>Then you just ask like you normally would:</p> <p>The files land in .desk/out/<job>/ with a short note on who did what, the scores and the cost.</p> <p>To pass, every axis needs 8 or more and the average needs 8.5. Fail-proof, and it goes back to the builder with the screenshot. A builder that misses the same note twice hands the file up to a senior, and a senior that misses twice gets one round with the Art Director. After the round cap, the job comes back marked under the bar, with a note on which axis fell short, so it won't quietly ship something that didn't pass.</p> <p>Here's a real terminal run of exactly that, on OpenAI models this time. Proof caught a type-scale problem in round 2, the builder fixed it, and round 3 still came back under the bar cause originality only got a 6. The last lines say what's missing.</p> <p>Splitting out the pick was deliberate. Once a direction is picked, every round after that is a fix to that one design, so a note like "type sizes, not layout" means the next round touches type sizes and nothing else. When every round is a fresh design, there's nothing steady to measure against, which was the whole problem in the first place.</p> <p>Proof has no model in it for a similar reason. Contrast against the real pixels, text spilling out of a box, a headline sitting in a platform's crop zone, a script checks all that the same way every time and it costs nothing. The models get to spend their judgment on the stuff a script can't see.</p> <p>This is the launch card for Desk Studio itself, retold from its job record.</p> <p>The UI Designer made three roughs: an editorial split, a type-only one, and a framed one. The Art Director went with rough 2, the type-only one, and wrote why: "headline reads first at both sizes, only amber is the small lamp, fixes are type sizes not layout."</p> <p>You can overrule that. Every rough has a Pick this button, and if you use it, the pick goes on record as yours instead of the Art Director's.</p> <p>After that, the builder polished, proof ran every round, and the Creative Director scored each one.</p> <p>originality 7, under the bar, back to polish</p> <p>Round 3 got a 9 on seven axes and an 8 on originality, so 8.9 on average. This is the file it signed off.</p> <p>The whole job came to $1.34 at list price.</p> <p>About 60% of that went to judgment and 40% to making, and the three polish rounds together were ten cents. That's what the tiers are for. If you're on a subscription, it's a list-price estimate of usage, not an extra bill.</p> <p>Before the Creative Director ever sees a file, proof renders it in Chrome at each target size and checks:</p> <p>You can also run proof on its own against any HTML file:</p> <p>1.1 rebuilt the dashboard into the floor you can leave open while a job runs. It only listens on 127.0.0.1 , and the URL carries a token.</p> <p>The strip at the top is the job. In this capture of the launch card, it's sitting on round 2's sign-off; round 1 came in at 8.4, $0.77 is spent so far, and it's 17m 25s in.</p> <p>Pause at next step holds the job before the next step, and Stop job ends it there. Neither one cuts a desk off halfway.</p> <p>Below that is the floor, with a room per tier and a Proof booth. Each desk is a little bot that wakes up while that desk is working and goes back to sleep after. A ×3 on a desk means three of them are running at once, which is what you see during the roughs. Every room's sign shows its model, and Change swaps the whole tier.</p> <p>Clicking a desk opens its panel. The UI Designer's panel here says it's on anthropic/haiku and has done 4 runs on this job, 887k tokens, $0.45. You can switch just that desk to another model, for this job or as the default, or leave it a note that goes into its next prompt.</p> <p>On the right is who's working right now, and under it the studio log in plain words. One line from this job reads "Creative Director scored round 1: 8.4, under the bar", and the polish for round 2 starts on the very next line.</p> <p>The roles and cost panel is where the tiers make sense. The builders went through 2.9 million tokens on this job, and that still came to ten cents. The slowest single run was the Creative Director's round 2 sign-off at 11 minutes 25 seconds, which tells you where the time actually goes.</p> <p>Since 1.0.2, a job's event log also exports as an OpenTelemetry trace, with role timings, tokens and cost, so a design job can sit in the same tracing tool as the rest of your stuff.</p> <p>The repo keeps a gallery of 17 signed-off pieces with their renders, scores and costs. Most are for four made-up brands, one's for a real site whose brand the studio found in the project, and three are for Desk Studio itself.</p> <p>The scores come from the studio's own model reviewers. They're useful for comparing rounds of one job, not as a benchmark against anything else. The standalone runner only takes design for social cards right now, and the rest of the commands are Claude Code skills. The briefs install into other agents fine, though not every command works the same way there yet.</p> <p>Free, MIT licensed, and it runs on the CLI login or API key you already have.</p> <p>Then ask your agent for a launch card and keep the floor open. The code, docs, and full gallery are on GitHub, and there's a 50-second film on deskstudio.ai.</p> <p>What I use most is the rounds view. I pull up round 1 next to round 3 and check if the thing I asked for is the thing that changed.</p> <p>I Marked My Hero Image fetchpriority="high" - The Browser Still Asked for It 1.5 Seconds Late</p> <p>I work on slow clicks and missing browser traces. I'm an OpenTelemetry Browser approver.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://hackernoon.com/i-put-a-42-desk-design-studio-inside-my-coding-agent?source=rss" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9775"> <h2>#9775. What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2023-10/Piloncillo.jpg" alt="What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>This article is part of our feature celebrating Pan Dulce. Find all things pan dulce here.</p> <p>Categorically, piloncillo is a “non-centrifugal” cane sugar, meaning it is an unrefined sugar product and a true natural brown sugar. It’s mostly consumed in Mexico and Latin America, but a similar product can be found in Asia, known as jaggery in India. Though often lumped together, these unrefined dark sugars are very different from brown sugars on the market today, which have been refined to a large degree — in some cases, they’re actually just white sugar with coloring or molasses added.</p> <p>Making piloncillo, on the other hand, involves an artisanal process that’s hundreds of years old. To make it, pressed cane juice is boiled to evaporate the water and deeply caramelize the sugar. The cooked cane is then poured into molds (often made of wood) and left to dry and harden. Traditional piloncillo is conical in shape and can vary in size from small to large cones but is most commonly found in a medium size that weighs about 200 grams. In Guatemala and Colombia, it is called panela, where it is cooked to a lighter degree and typically formed into a brick, rather than cone, shape. Other forms of piloncillo can be granulated or liquid (which is more rare).</p> <p>Minimally processed and boldly flavored, piloncillo was historically a prized and respected foodstuff. As an unrefined cane sugar, piloncillo provides more complex vitamins and minerals than refined sugars, which undergo processing and whitening methods that also strip nutrients from the whole food. And piloncillo is also great for baking, providing notes of burnt caramel and hints of smoke. Plus, its rich molasses qualities keep baked goods moist and fresh for longer.</p> <p>Always look at the ingredient label when purchasing piloncillo and make sure it says 100% pure cane juice or cane sugar. It is becoming increasingly common to find imitation products marketed as jaggery or piloncillo that contain coloring and corn syrup. You can find good piloncillo at specialty grocery stores or online at retailers.</p> <p>In Mexico and throughout Latin America, piloncillo is an important ingredient in many traditional dishes. (Some will even say it’s not the “real dish” if you substitute sugar in these recipes due to the deep flavors and richness that only piloncillo can provide.) This deep, dark unrefined sugar lends its characteristic flavor and texture to popular foods and beverages such as capirotada, tepache, coyotas, atole, café de olla, calabaza al horno, coricos, and hojarascas, to name a few!</p> <p>I love adding piloncillo when I’m making champurrado. In this warm and thick chocolate beverage, the piloncillo is chopped or grated and dissolved in the pot with water or milk before adding the chocolate and masa. In this recipe, the piloncillo’s intense sweet and smoky flavors pair well with the chocolate and corn masa.</p> <p>While there are many dishes and uses for piloncillo, it’s not a simple substitution for granulated white sugar in recipes, but you can use it the same as you would brown sugar with a 1:1 substitution by weight.  Depending on how hard the cone is, it can be crumbled or grated for easier measuring. If it is very hard, try cutting it in half with a sharp knife and then placing it between parchment paper or a towel and beating with a rolling pin.</p> <p>Find puerquitos and many more Mexican sweets in our feature celebrating pan dulce.</p> <p>Cover photo by Rick Holbrook; food styling by Kaitlin Wayne.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>It’s a sweet (and confusing) world out there, so we’re breaking it all down.</p> <p>Fewer calories, but do they yield great results?</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/01/piloncillo" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9774"> <h2>#9774. margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/5-costco-baked-goods-to-buy-and-4-to-skip/l-intro-1794238065.jpg" alt="5 Costco Baked Goods To Buy And 4 To Skip" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.</p> <p>The holidays are just around the corner. Between Thanksgiving and Christmas, you'll have Friendsgivings, work parties, school functions, and every other conceivable event that may require you to bring a baked good. Sometimes, it's a bit too much, which is why there's absolutely no shame in going the store-bought route instead of firing up the oven at home.</p> <p>Prices are as of the date of publication and may vary based on region.</p> <p>Costco is a godsend if you're hosting a large group for brunch. There are a handful of breakfast-centric items on this list, but first and foremost are the bagels. I snagged a bag of the plain bagels, but Costco has several other flavors, including Parmesan Cheese and the new Pretzel Bagels.</p> <p>An 8-pack of Plain Bagels retails for $5.66, an unsurprisingly great value given the store. True to form, the bagels are also quite large, making them worthy of a full meal on their own. While they don't come pre-sliced, I prefer to buy bagels whole as it helps keep them fresh. Each bagel is soft, chewy, and toasts up perfectly.</p> <p>If bagels are the main focus of your meal, there's no need to overthink things. Costco bagels are great, even if they don't come from a shop focused entirely on them. This is the perfect, no-stress addition to any breakfast and a definite freezer staple.</p> <p>Because our relationship is built on trust, I'm going to come right out and say the "skips" on this list aren't hard passes, but more likely items you can survive without. Frankly, Costco doesn't make many bad products, and the Buttermilk Biscuits are one such example.</p> <p>These things are huge. I honestly don't think I've ever seen a biscuit this large, let alone ten of them for $7.93. I'll jump into the review in a moment, but the reason the biscuits landed in my skip pile is that they're one of the few baked goods I purchased that came with cooking instructions and the only one that I think really needs to be cooked to be properly enjoyed.</p> <p>A cold biscuit is, in my opinion, a sad biscuit, and while Costco's Buttermilk Biscuits are serviceable at room temperature, they're worlds better when warmed up. You can toss them in the oven or do what I did and zap each one in the microwave for about 30 seconds. The result is a steaming, fluffy, buttery biscuit roughly the size of a baseball. These are really good biscuits, but if they need to be warm to really enjoy them, there are more convenient options in the Costco bakery.</p> <p>France has delivered a lot of wonderful things to the United States — looking at you, Lady Liberty — but the best cultural exchange may have been the croissant. Almost impossibly airy, flaky, and absurdly buttery, the croissant is a hugely versatile pastry. It can go sweet, it can go savory, or you can just munch on one as a snack.</p> <p>A 12-pack of Costco Croissants is just $6.80. For comparison, my local Target has an 8-pack of Pillsbury Original Crescent Rolls for $3.39. Don't get me wrong, I love those fresh-baked little bundles of joy, but a single Costco croissant is equivalent to multiple of the smaller home-baked ones. The value is unbeatable, and the flavor is close behind. These croissants are everything you could hope for, and, thanks to their size, you can really get creative with them. Slice one in half and make a sandwich or, as I did, take 8 and put them into a fantastic French toast bake. It's culinary cultural inception and a great way to use a very tasty baked good.</p> <p>Costco's muffins have a long and surprisingly winding history filled with recipe and size changes that bordered on national scandals. Thankfully, it seems that the muffins have once again found their sweet spot as some of the better options from the Costco bakery. Of course, this is a skip, though, so while I enjoy the Vanilla Chocolate Chip Muffins (which retail for $7.93 for an 8-count package), you can do better.</p> <p>Costco has a number of different muffin flavors. Blueberry, Vanilla Chocolate Chip, and Double Chocolate are the standard options, but seasonal and rotating offerings include everything from Blueberry Creme to Pumpkin Streusel. I've reviewed Costco's Double Chocolate Muffins before and they're fantastic; rich, filled with chocolate, and riding that fine line between a breakfast pastry and a dessert.</p> <p>The Vanilla Chocolate Chip Muffins are plenty tasty in their own right. Each one is remarkably soft and spongy, with a sweetness that makes it taste like a supersized Little Debbie treat. The chocolate chips are large, but not super evenly distributed. These are perfectly serviceable muffins you're almost guaranteed to enjoy, but Costco has better muffins, so these are an easy skip.</p> <p>Let's start with the fact that this pack has not one, but two coconut-based bars. The Wildberry Macaroons are admittedly tasty thanks to a tart berry jam that rests between a bevy of toasted coconut flakes and a soft, buttery macaroon base. Yes, that's double coconut in one bar, but a single, good coconut option is just fine by me. The issue is that the Macaroon Madness Bars are a second coconut-based treat disguised as a blondie. Until I took a bite, I had no idea that this bar was also filled with coconut. It's not as good or as interesting as the Wildberry Macaroon, so this feels like a total waste of space.</p> <p>The Artisan Rolls are sold in a 12-pack for $6.80. They're precut and, you guessed it, they're big. The ciabatta-style bread is chewy, airy, and perfect for sandwiches. Especially leftover sandwiches. Perhaps after a food-centric holiday. What I'm getting at is that you need to buy these for the day after Thanksgiving to make some spectacular, carbtastic, leftover sandwiches. They're hearty enough to handle whatever combination of turkey, gravy, potatoes, stuffing, and cranberry sauce you can throw at them, but not so dense that you'll fill up on bread. A good roll in the right setting can make a meal, and Costco's Artisan Rolls are perfect for making the kind of sandwich that inevitably leads to a wonderful nap.</p> <p>I've waxed poetic about Costco's portion sizes thus far because, for the most part, I can find a way to normalize a massive amount of baked goods in the right setting. There is an exception to every rule, though, and the baguette is mine.</p> <p>Priced at $5.66 for a two-pack of baguettes, this is an almost absurd amount of bread. Each baguette is nearly two feet long. Combined, that's the height of a 6-year-old. Unlike some of the other items I tried, the baguette also seems to have the shortest shelf life. You either need to eat it that day or freeze it immediately to avoid the outer crust from becoming chewy. If you're hosting a spaghetti dinner that night, this is a decent enough option, but it's still a bread that simply doesn't stay good for long.</p> <p>I'm not entirely out on the Costco Baguette, but beyond being generally impractical, it's not a product that blew me away with either taste or texture. It's fine, and with so many other things to choose from, fine isn't enough.</p> <p>In the world of sweet breakfast pastries, I think the Danish is too often forgotten. It's basically the flaky, buttery goodness of a croissant paired with pie filling. Honestly, how could that combo ever be bad?</p> <p>Costco's danishes come in packs of four. There are a few unique flavors to choose from, with Cheese, Cherry, and Almond as the standards, while seasonal favorites include Strawberry Cream Cheese and Apple Cinnamon. The mix-and-match portion of the name comes from the pricing: You can get two four-packs for $13.61, which is what I did to end up with a Cheese and an Apple.</p> <p>True to form, these Danishes are hefty and really tasty. The fillings are sweet, but not overwhelmingly so, and the pastry portion is baked to perfection. The Cheese flavor is especially great for anyone who lives on the more savory side of the spectrum, but still likes to dabble in the occasional sweet treat. The Apple was my favorite, though. I like any excuse to eat a classic apple pie for breakfast, and Costco's Danish is the perfect one.</p> <p>I purchased all nine Costco baked goods at the same time and brought them home to photograph and sample. My evaluations were based on flavor, texture, and overall value.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2310868/costco-baked-goods-buy-skip/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9770"> <h2>#9770. RevOps Is Quietly Becoming an Engineering Job</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/FrXwz2OOpLRbd0xvRNk08vBI1oo1-3483bcd.jpeg" alt="RevOps Is Quietly Becoming an Engineering Job" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Over the last two weeks, I've written here about a calendar table that knows November 1 has 25 hours, a customer health score that barely beats a coin flip, a 1961 warehouse formula that finds dead deals in a CRM, a Slack report that checks its own numbers before it posts, an exam for AI agents, a macOS job that died because of where it kept its log file, and why 3x pipeline coverage is a guess.</p> <p>My title is Head of Revenue Operations. Very little of that shows up in a RevOps job description.</p> <p>I started in supply chain, moved into revenue operations, and taught myself SQL along the way. For most of that time, the job looked the way people describe it: own the CRM, build the reports, run the forecast, keep sales and finance looking at the same numbers. That's still the job. But the way it gets done has changed, and I think it's changing faster than the job descriptions.</p> <p>The data moved into the warehouse. RevOps used to live inside the CRM and its report builder. Now the numbers that matter, from billing, product usage, payments, and the CRM itself, land in Snowflake or BigQuery. The person who reconciles them needs SQL, not a report wizard.</p> <p>Writing code got cheap. An AI coding agent will write the script that syncs the CRM, builds the workbook, or posts the report in minutes. That's the real shift. When code is cheap, more of RevOps becomes code, and someone has to run it.</p> <p>Running it is the part that didn't get cheaper. A script is easy. A script that runs at 7:45 every morning for two years, survives a laptop update, posts nothing when the data is wrong, and tells someone when it didn't run at all: that's operations engineering. And it's increasingly a RevOps problem, because the scripts are about revenue and nobody else owns them.</p> <p>If you work in RevOps, sales ops, or finance ops and you're wondering where to invest, here's my list, roughly in order of how often each one has saved me.</p> <p>SQL, properly. Not just SELECT and GROUP BY. Grain, joins that duplicate rows, window functions, time zones. Most wrong numbers I've chased came down to a join or a day boundary. (These six Snowflake patterns cover the ones I reach for every week.)</p> <p>One scheduler, and how it fails. cron, launchd, GitHub Actions, Airflow. Pick the one you'll actually use and learn what it does when things go wrong. Every scheduler has a way to fail silently. Know yours.</p> <p>Version control for anything that produces a number. If it ends up in front of a CFO, it goes in git. "Which version of the query made that slide?" should have an answer.</p> <p>Testing numbers, not just code. Reconciliations, check cells, golden questions with known answers. Code that runs is not code that's right.</p> <p>Staging and promotion. Somewhere to break things that isn't production, and a deliberate step between the two.</p> <p>Writing definitions down. Every metric needs a written definition that sales and finance have both agreed to. It's the least technical item on this list, and the one that prevents the most arguments.</p> <p>Working with AI agents. Give them a sandbox, an exam, and a short list of things they're never allowed to touch. Then let them do a lot of the typing.</p> <p>The risk in all of this is that RevOps turns into a shadow data engineering team: pipelines nobody else understands, a dozen scheduled jobs on one laptop, and a single person who knows how any of it works. That version is worse than not automating at all.</p> <p>So draw a line. Data engineering owns the platform: ingestion, the warehouse, the infrastructure everyone shares. RevOps owns the business logic and the last mile: the definitions, the reconciliations, the reports, and the small automations that move revenue numbers to the people who use them.</p> <p>And give the last mile an exit. When a RevOps automation becomes important enough that its failure would hurt the company, it graduates to the platform, with real monitoring, an owner on call, and a second person who understands it.</p> <p>Most RevOps postings still ask for CRM administration, reporting, and strong analytical skills. Those matter. But the people I see doing this job well now are also comfortable in a terminal, can read a stack trace without panic, and treat a scheduled job like a product with users.</p> <p>The title still says operations. More and more, the work says engineering. The people who do well will be the ones who take both words seriously.</p> <p>The pieces mentioned at the top, with runnable code, are on my HackerNoon profile.</p> <p>I'm Malek Damiri, head of revenue operations in Atlanta. I write about revenue operations and the systems behind it at malekdamiri.com.</p> <p>How to Generate, Recalculate, and Validate Excel Workbooks With Python</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://hackernoon.com/revops-is-quietly-becoming-an-engineering-job?source=rss" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9769"> <h2>#9769. Not American Or Cheddar: Grab This Cheese For Perfect Breakfast Sandwiches (Thanks, Martha Stewart)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/not-american-or-cheddar-grab-this-cheese-for-perfect-breakfast-sandwiches-thanks-martha-stewart/l-intro-1793973236.jpg" alt="Not American Or Cheddar: Grab This Cheese For Perfect Breakfast Sandwiches (Thanks, Martha Stewart)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Practical, budget-friendly, and endlessly versatile, sandwiches are an everyday staple for a reason. Though there's no right or one way to do them, certain combinations have proven to be instant crowd-pleasers. Enter the humble bacon, egg, and cheese, the breakfast of champions and Bobby Flay's favorite late-night snack. It sounds simple enough, but the ingredients you use and how you treat them can be the difference between standard deli fare and Michelin-worthy grub. If you like the sound of the latter option, borrow a tip from the icon herself, Martha Stewart, and use fontina cheese next time you're making one.</p> <p>Fontina is a must-try Italian cheese. Originating from the Aosta Valley in the Italian Alps, it's a semi-soft cow's milk cheese that's been produced since the 12th century. Its high fat content is responsible for its creamy texture, accompanied by a mild nutty and earthy flavor that intensifies with age. Beyond these already impressive attributes, the thing that makes it so well-suited to a bacon, egg, and cheese is its melting capability. You'll have no trouble finding it in Italian dishes like fonduta alla Valdostana (Italy's answer to fondue) and polenta concia, where it's melted down into a thick, gooey consistency with polenta, milk, and butter. Martha Stewart also pairs fontina with pizza on a pie that features lemon and rosemary (via YouTube).</p> <p>There are many versions of fontina available, but for the most traditional, pick up Fontina DOP, which is made from raw, whole milk of native Valdostana cattle breeds fed on alpine grass or hay. Because it uses raw milk, it must be aged past the USDA's required 60 days. To put it all together, take a cue from Martha Stewart and use an English muffin as your base. Toast it until golden, then layer on crispy bacon and eggs cooked to your liking. While the eggs are still hot, add a slice or two of fontina and let the residual heat melt the cheese into a creamy, gooey layer.</p> <p>A bacon, egg, and cheese paired with fontina is already a winning combination, but there are a few ways to make it even better. For quick melting and an extra hit of creamy flavor, place the fontina on your bread and give it a blast under the broiler. You can also pop your bacon under there to get it extra crispy, but hold off on adding the egg until afterward. It's delicate, after all, and can quickly overcook under such intense heat. On that note, keep a close eye on your cheese as it broils — there's a fine line between beautifully melted and golden and burnt beyond saving.</p> <p>Beyond breakfast sandwiches, you can also use fontina to make another classic: grilled cheese. Given its excellent reputation for meltability, adding fontina to a grilled cheese is practically a no-brainer. You don't have to stop at bread and cheese, either. If you want to put a twist on the classic grilled cheese and tomato soup pairing, tuck in a few slices of tomato and some fresh basil leaves.</p> <p>In a nod to its Italian heritage, fontina is also a welcome addition to a panini. Your idea of a panini might depend on where you are in the world. In Italy, panino simply means sandwich, and often features a more restrained combination of cured meats, cheese, and vegetables than its U.S. counterpart. So if you want the fontina to shine, take a little inspiration from its homeland. Try layering it with thinly sliced prosciutto, roasted red peppers, and a few leaves of peppery arugula on ciabatta. Add a drizzle of olive oil and a little freshly cracked black pepper and sea salt, then use a panini press until the bread is crisp and the cheese has melted.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2308951/not-american-cheddar-creamy-cheese-perfect-breakfast-sandwich-martha-stewart/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9768"> <h2>#9768. 16 pumpkin recipes, from cakes and cookies to bars and bread: We've got a marbled pumpkin cake, chewy pumpkin cookies, and even pumpkin milk bread.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/Pumpkin-Snickerdoodle-Cookies_FALL-26_BOTW_2026_Action_H_0693.jpg" alt="16 pumpkin recipes, from cakes and cookies to bars and bread: We've got a marbled pumpkin cake, chewy pumpkin cookies, and even pumpkin milk bread." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>It’s that time of year when pumpkin spice everything starts appearing on store shelves — candles, lip balm, air fresheners, beer, and of course, the ubiquitous PSL (pumpkin spice latte). That means fall is here, and more importantly, that pumpkin should make a grand return to your kitchen! Pull out your canned pumpkin — or better yet, make your own pumpkin purée — and stock your pantry with pumpkin pie spice, because we have the best pumpkin recipes to bake this fall.</p> <p>This Pumpkin Swirl Cake takes my breath away every time I unmold it from its intricate loaf pan. The anticipation keeps building until I slice into the pound cake-like loaf and reveal the swirled pattern inside, marbled with both vanilla and spiced pumpkin batter. (Don’t fret if you don’t have the specialty loaf pan — this can also be baked in a standard loaf pan and adorned with a simple confectioners’ sugar icing.)</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Patch O Pumpkins Loaf Pan and Pure Vanilla Plus</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice and Sparkling Sugar</p> <p>A cousin of Belgian-style Liège waffles, these Pumpkin Sugar Crunch Waffles have caramelized edges and a pleasant chew that’s reminiscent of brioche. The yeasted batter has pumpkin in it for flavor and color, plus Swedish pearl sugar that melts into pockets of crispy sugar. The best part? The batter rests overnight, so if you prepare it the night ahead, all you have to do the next morning is scoop and cook the batter for hot, crispy waffles in just a few minutes.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Sugar Crunch Waffles</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Swedish Pearl Sugar</p> <p>I used to make the same pumpkin pie recipe for years, and it always left me wanting a little more excitement. Then I found this Smooth and Spicy Pumpkin Pie and never looked back! The generously spiced filling uses nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and Vietnamese cinnamon to create a more flavorful pie than traditional versions. The secret to its silky-smooth texture? Corn syrup, which is an invert sugar and keeps the custard from becoming grainy. Substitute another invert sugar like honey or maple syrup if you like; I use maple syrup.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Smooth and Spicy Pumpkin Pie</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Vietnamese Cinnamon, Ginger, and Nutmeg</p> <p>Whenever I have these tender, golden scones on hand, I look forward to getting out of bed the next morning because I know they’re waiting for me. They can be easily customized to use a range of mix-ins, depending on what you have in your pantry. My personal preference is a mix of crystallized ginger and Cinnamon Sweet Bits.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Harvest Pumpkin Scones (or Gluten-Free Pumpkin Scones)</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Mini Diced Ginger and Cinnamon Sweet Bits</p> <p>If you’re looking for a way to make your whole kitchen smell like fall, these one-bowl, easy pumpkin muffins deliver — and fast. They’re ready in under an hour, so you can spend less time measuring, mixing, and cleaning and more time tackling your autumn bucket list.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Standard Muffin Pan</p> <p>Making banana bread is an almost weekly activity in my house — except during fall, when we pivot to pumpkin bread instead. This is a quick, easy bake that satisfies my craving for something pumpkin-y, and it uses a simple trick to concentrate the pumpkin flavor and ensure the loaf is perfectly textured: The pumpkin purée is reduced on the stovetop to cook off excess moisture. (The process is similar to browning butter.) As a result, the final loaf is packed with pumpkin flavor.</p> <p>Get the recipe: The Most Pumpkin Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Bread</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Ginger and Semisweet Chocolate Chips</p> <p>These bars have all the cozy, spiced goodness of the classic dessert in a portable, crowd-friendly form. The buttery, brown sugar crust gets pressed into the pan (no rolling out pie dough!), and the silky pumpkin filling comes together with just a handful of ingredients. The (optional but highly recommended) sour cream whipped topping brings a slight tanginess and completes the traditional pumpkin pie experience.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice</p> <p>This Pumpkin Milk Bread is exceptionally soft, squishy, and feather-light, while also packing in a lot of pumpkin. Pumpkin can often weigh down baked goods, but here the combination of a tangzhong, bread flour, and a long mix makes this bread simultaneously moist and high-rising.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Instant Yeast</p> <p>This tender pumpkin crumb cake is for people who double the chocolate chips in pumpkin bread and the streusel on coffee cake. Atop the thin layer of spiced pumpkin cake lays a heavy blanket of buttery crumbs with a bold chocolate flavor, thanks to Dutch-processed cocoa powder.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Chocolate-Pumpkin Crumb Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Black Cocoa</p> <p>These Pumpkin Cupcakes, with their piped swirl of cream cheese frosting, are the ideal way to celebrate fall birthdays. The cupcakes are super tender, thanks to the addition of cake flour and oil. Sour cream and brown sugar add tanginess and molasses-y sweetness while also preventing the cupcakes from being dry.</p> <p>For more cupcake decorating ideas, see our YouTube video: Decorate Cupcakes Better Than Ever.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Cake Flour (or Gluten-Free Measure for Measure Flour)</p> <p>My husband’s favorite fall dessert is Pumpkin Whoopie Pies, hands down. He can’t resist these subtly sweet cakes sandwiching rich cream cheese filling. This recipe has a few extra bells and whistles to take it over the top: Bread and Cake Enhancer to keep the cakes extra soft and fresh, xanthan gum in the filling to give it a smooth mouthfeel, and diced crystallized ginger for a bit of extra zing in the filling.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Bread and Cake Enhancer, Xanthan Gum, and Mini Diced Ginger</p> <p>The next time there’s a rainy weekend, I’m taking on a project bake: our Pumpkin Cream Cheese Danish. It’s a multiday process and laminating dough is a labor of love, but the final product is worth the effort: buttery, crisp pastries filled with pumpkin and sweet cream cheese.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Cream Cheese Danish</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Baker’s Special Dry Milk</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice</p> <p>This Pumpkin Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting is a show-stopping dessert featuring spiced layers of cake, not-too-sweet cream cheese frosting, and a blanket of melted caramel poured over the top. Will it be slightly messy to serve? Yes. Will anyone mind? Absolutely not.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice and Offset Spatula</p> <p>The pumpkin spice recipe I’m most excited to bake this fall is a mash-up of greats: Part-coffee cake, part-Bundt cake, part-pumpkin bread, this Pumpkin Espresso Bundt Cake deserves a category all of its own. It has two layers of espresso swirl tucked within a moist, spiced cake. Make it in your favorite Bundt pan or serve it as a loaf if you’re more of simple-is-better person. Either way, it’s great for snacking all day long.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Espresso Bundt Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Espresso Powder and Bundt Pan</p> <p>For more recipes that are ideal to bake as the seasons change, see our collection of Fall Favorites.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Recipes posts.</p> <p>It’s peak baking season — here’s what to make.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/05/pumpkin-recipes" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9767"> <h2>#9767. Claude Meetings</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Add Claude to your call and get work started as you talk </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/claude?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1314781?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/claude" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9766"> <h2>#9766. Ganella</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; color: #333;"> <p><p> Your Mac Dock, with live widgets for the apps you use </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/ganella?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1312991?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/ganella" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9765"> <h2>#9765. 11 Fast Food Chains With Onion Rings On The Menu</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/11-fast-food-chains-with-onion-rings-on-the-menu/l-intro-1793994987.jpg" alt="11 Fast Food Chains With Onion Rings On The Menu" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>If you're dining at a fast food restaurant, especially one that serves hamburgers, then you may be used to getting your order with a side of fries. Most chains offer this as a default side dish (we've even ranked the best ones), especially with their combo meals, and some of the biggest names in fast food have limited alternatives to the crispy fried potatoes. But what do you do if you don't want spuds at a fast food joint?</p> <p>Fortunately, there are many restaurants that offer alternatives. Below are 11 fast food chains, from big national (and international) names to more regional ones, that offer a variety of onion ring styles — some of which are considered among the best available, according to customers. You'll find everything from breaded to batter-fried, whole onion to minced onion, and even a variety that is extra sweet thanks to a rumored special ingredient in the coating. Just keep in mind that prices may vary depending on the location.</p> <p>Burger King is perhaps the biggest fast food chain that offers onion rings on its menu. They're distinct in that they're made with minced onion combined with a batter, though there are reports that BK in Canada allegedly changed the recipe to resemble traditional onion rings in 2026. The advantage of this chain's method of preparing onion rings is that it results in a uniform texture in each bite, rather than the onion slipping away from the breading.</p> <p>Onion rings are available at Burger King for $3.99.</p> <p>Cook Out is a regional chain of fast food restaurants primarily concentrated in the Southeastern United States, with most of its locations in North Carolina. The chain's onion rings are part of its selection of sides, though if you order a tray, you'll get your choice of two sides. You can even double up on rings if you wish.</p> <p>A side of onion rings costs $1.99 at Cook Out.</p> <p>In 1921, White Castle opened its first store, and while the chain is best known for its small sliders, it also has onion rings on its menu in some locations. According to customers, they're easy to eat and packed with oniony flavor, with one Redditor proclaiming that "White [Castle] o-rings are the best." If you're not a fan of ring-shaped food, though, you can also opt for onion chips available at some locations.</p> <p>Onion rings are available at some White Castle locations for $3.19.</p> <p>Carl's Jr. has its locations primarily in the western United States and is known for its smiling star logo. The chain has a variety of sides you can choose from to accompany its burgers, and onion rings are one of them. They are breaded instead of batter-fried and come with your choice of one of six dipping sauces.</p> <p>Onion rings are available at Carl's Jr. for $5.04.</p> <p>Hardee's can be seen as Carl's Jr.'s sister brand, except that while the latter's locations are principally in the western United States, it has most of its locations in the eastern part of the country. While they both share the same cute star logo, regional menu variations mean not every item is identical, including how each chain markets its sides. For example, Hardee's explicitly advertises its version as "Beer-Battered Onion Rings," whereas Carl's Jr. simply lists it as "Onion Rings" on the menu.</p> <p>You can order Beer-Battered Onion Rings at Hardee's for $3.79.</p> <p>The A&W brand all started with a root beer stand that opened in 1919 in Lodi, California, and now its locations are scattered across the U.S. The chain's onion rings are made with white onions that are breaded before being fried to render them crispy, and some customers comment on their delicious seasoning, while others love their crunchiness.</p> <p>Onion rings are available at A&W for $3.49.</p> <p>Some onion rings are breaded, while others are dipped in batter before being fried, which gives them a smoother texture, and this is how Whataburger makes its onion rings, according to customers. The Texas-based chain, which is seemingly everywhere now, also offers a variety of dipping sauces to choose from, including gravy and its signature Fancy Ketchup.</p> <p>A medium order of onion rings is available at Whataburger for $4.49.</p> <p>While most of its locations are on the West Coast, Jack in the Box has a significant presence in Texas and a scattering of stores throughout the country. The onion rings here stand out because they're coated in Japanese-style panko breadcrumbs, which give them a crispy texture, and customers agree that it makes all the difference.</p> <p>Onion rings are available at Jack in the Box for $3.99.</p> <p>Culver's is a chain originally from Wisconsin and has a cult following in the Midwest, where it has the most locations. Besides serving some of Reddit's favorite fast food hamburgers, it's also known for its sides. And while many customers opt for its cheese curds — a local specialty — the chain also has fans of its onion rings, which are made from whole white onions and are batter-fried. Customers also love how you can get Ken's Boom Boom sauce here for dipping.</p> <p>Onion rings are available at Culver's for $3.49.</p> <p>Many may associate Dairy Queen with its soft-serve ice cream and other frozen treats, but in the '60s, the chain actually debuted its Brazier program, which included savory items, like burgers, at some of its locations. This was eventually replaced by the DQ Grill & Chill concept, which is where you can order onion rings. One Reddit user even claims that "they are breaded and resemble steakhouse onion rings."</p> <p>Onion rings are available at participating Dairy Queens for $3.29.</p> <p>While most fast food chains are known for their drive-thru lanes, there is one that's known for offering customers an old-school drive-in dining experience: Sonic. Customers are particularly fond of its onion rings, which are reportedly sweeter thanks to a breading that some online liken to the flavor of cake batter. Rumors circulate that the chain uses vanilla ice cream mix in the coating, though the chain has never officially confirmed this.</p> <p>Onion rings are available at Sonic for $4.29.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2309645/what-fast-food-chains-serve-onion-rings-menu/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9764"> <h2>#9764. Aven App Agent</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> AI that guides users through your app </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/aven-app-agent?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1313374?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/aven-app-agent" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9763"> <h2>#9763. Burnstate</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Claude Code, Codex & Cursor limits, paced in your menu bar </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/burnstate?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1311191?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/burnstate" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9762"> <h2>#9762. Top 10 AI Tools That Will Transform Your Content Creation in 2025</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><div style="text-align: left;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEge5QgwLKWbavTUhIedQLI79z5BGD4h0ZoH4YMK6bGBL6fY4Je8R3GZurMZaJmtYirFS6pS-GgZD3xFAqfln8w8faEY2iDehndQNeez57DoiDsgYFJrIwMOLBjzcZiOJrqYDktm6pmRkwtprJChag0yQoeEZx1Pa_eKnt3kKzz69f-FSPWu_JXQxFq5Z8WZ/s1920/Blue%20Purple%20Futuristic%20Modern%203D%20Tech%20Company%20Business%20Presentation.jpg" style="clear: left; margin-bottom: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Coda;"><img alt="Top 10 AI Tools That Will Transform Your Content Creation in 2025" border="0" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEge5QgwLKWbavTUhIedQLI79z5BGD4h0ZoH4YMK6bGBL6fY4Je8R3GZurMZaJmtYirFS6pS-GgZD3xFAqfln8w8faEY2iDehndQNeez57DoiDsgYFJrIwMOLBjzcZiOJrqYDktm6pmRkwtprJChag0yQoeEZx1Pa_eKnt3kKzz69f-FSPWu_JXQxFq5Z8WZ/s16000/Blue%20Purple%20Futuristic%20Modern%203D%20Tech%20Company%20Business%20Presentation.jpg" title="Top 10 AI Tools That Will Transform Your Content Creation in 2025" /></span></a></div><p><span style="font-family: Coda;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;">Looking to level up your content creation game in 2025? You're in the right place! The digital landscape has evolved dramatically, and AI tools have become essential for creators who want to stay ahead of the curve. Please verify current details with the respective platforms, Also this article contain affiliate links which means we make a small comission if yo buy any premium plan from our links</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Coda;">Pricing updated on 01/02/ 2025 </span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Coda;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;"><br /></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;"><br /></span></p><p><br /></p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://techncruncher.blogspot.com/2025/01/top-10-ai-tools-that-will-transform.html" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9761"> <h2>#9761. Forget Mayo: Spread This Rich Ingredient On Bread For A More Flavorful Grilled Cheese</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/forget-mayo-spread-this-rich-ingredient-on-bread-for-a-more-flavorful-grilled-cheese/l-intro-1794210409.jpg" alt="Forget Mayo: Spread This Rich Ingredient On Bread For A More Flavorful Grilled Cheese" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Butter gives your grilled cheese great richness, and using mayo makes it far crispier, but neither adds a ton of strong flavors that can shine through high-quality cheese. That's why you need toum, a Lebanese garlic spread that delivers intense taste with very little effort.</p> <p>Toum is as rich as mayonnaise and as light and fluffy as whipped cream, created by smashing garlic into a paste and then gradually whipping in oil until it has an airy but glossy consistency. For texture, its incredible fluffiness makes it easy to slather on, covering every last inch in a swiftly melting browning agent that makes the bread crispy. But for flavoring, it makes the end product taste like garlic bread, full of rich fats and pungent aromatics that only requires a swift spread with a knife. It may seem like you're using a lot and will over-season your sandwich, but since so much of it is air, you're actually only using a moderate amount that's quite easy to thoroughly apply.</p> <p>The combination of melty gooeyness inside and crisp, garlicky exteriors is a second-to-none combination that pairs well with a wide variety of cheeses. Add in the sharpness of the lemon juice, and you get something that can brighten up even the heaviest, fat-laden cheeses quite well. The only caveat is that all that garlic gives it a fairly cool smoke point, so you'll need to use low to medium heat to avoid making it grow bitter.</p> <p>Since its main flavors are garlic and lemon, toum isn't quite as universal a pairing as mayonnaise or butter. It goes great with anything semi-hard and creamy, but its intensity may clash with anything stronger. You'll also want to know the type of oil used in your toum. Something made with grapeseed, canola, or other neutral varieties is far more compatible than a spread made with a flavorful extra virgin olive oil.</p> <p>Cheeses with a nuttier profile, like Jarlsberg, Gruyère, and Manchego, are all solid pairings. They tend to be a bit earthier, grounding the brightness of the toum, so it isn't too intense. Since it has no eggs, you can even combine it with melted vegan cheese since nutritional yeast is typically quite aromatic and nutty. Richer, well-rounded varieties can also be quite nice, so some shreds of gouda, raclette, and any triple-cream variety are always welcome additions.</p> <p>Flavored cheeses are one of the easiest ways to upgrade any melty sandwich, but not all are compatible with toum. While something rich in herbs or wine can complement the garlic quite well, a variety with a lot of sweetened fruit or more lemon can be a bit much. Since toum is already quite tangy, you may also want to steer clear of acidic cheeses like chèvre, feta, or cream cheese. While some may like the brightness, it can quickly become overly intense, and you may find yourself making a new sandwich.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2310415/forget-mayo-spread-rich-ingredient-bread-sandwich-more-flavorful-toum/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9760"> <h2>#9760. What are flour enzymes?: Understanding a common flour ingredient.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/flour%20enzymes%202.jpg" alt="What are flour enzymes?: Understanding a common flour ingredient." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>If you look closely at a bag of King Arthur flour, you may see an unfamiliar ingredient listed there: enzyme.</p> <p>We’re extremely thoughtful about every ingredient we use, across all King Arthur products and recipes. Our Food Philosophy guides every decision to ensure the quality of what we create, and that includes the enzymes in our flour.</p> <p>Here’s exactly what flour enzymes are and why they’re included in flour.</p> <p>Enzymes are found naturally in wheat, and thus are already present in flour. An enzyme is a protein produced by a living organism that acts as a catalyst to bring about a specific biochemical reaction.</p> <p>The amount of enzymes in flour can vary based on growing conditions from harvest to harvest and year to year, so we add natural enzymes to correct for any variance and make sure our flour bakes more consistently — in other words, to make your baking even better. Those enzymes make up a very small portion of the total flour: less than 1%.</p> <p>The enzyme we use in our flour is technically called fungal alpha-amylase. That’s a pretty technical name, so it is commonly labeled simply as “enzyme” on ingredient labels. “Alpha-amylase” is the actual enzyme, and “fungal” refers to the fact that the living organism that produces the enzyme is a fungus, not unlike yeast or a mushroom. Amylase may sound unfamiliar, but your body makes and uses it every day. When you eat, it begins breaking starch into smaller carbohydrates so you can draw on it for energy. Amylases added to flour perform a similar function.</p> <p>Note: Though fungi are technically living organisms, enzymes are considered vegan, as they are not animal based.</p> <p>Malted barley is an alternative source of enzymes that King Arthur has used in the past, but we found the efficacy can vary batch to batch. By swapping malted barley for straight enzymes, the flour produces more consistent results for our bakers.</p> <p>Another reason we made the switch? Enzymes require less water and energy to produce than malt barley. As a Certified B Corporation, we're committed to being good stewards of our planet, so pivoting to a responsibly sourced ingredient with a smaller environmental footprint makes sense.</p> <p>To put it simply, enzymes are added to flours to improve baking performance — they do not change the flour's nutritional value. More specifically, they help create the foods that feeds yeasts. The enzymes break down complex starches into simpler sugars; this, in turn, provides yeast with readily available fermentable sugar (food!), which enables yeast to work continuously and supports both fermentation and crust browning. This results in improved bread volume and crumb texture. Most other manufacturers of flour and yeasted mixes use enzymes for the very same reasons.</p> <p>Ultimately, enzymes are yet another way for us to provide you with the most consistent flour — which means even better baking.</p> <p>Cover photo and food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.</p> <p>A guide to baking with self-rising flour.</p> <p>The best baking starts with the best flour.</p> <p>It all comes down to gluten-forming protein content.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/15/flour-enzymes" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; GAtrends</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Spike alerts for your keywords in Telegram, Claude, ChatGPT </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/gatrends?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1314471?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/gatrends" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9758"> <h2>#9758. Leftover Fried Chicken Is Juicier With This 2-Step Reheating Method</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/leftover-fried-chicken-is-juicier-with-this-2-step-reheating-method/l-intro-1793906642.jpg" alt="Leftover Fried Chicken Is Juicier With This 2-Step Reheating Method" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Fried chicken is one of those dishes that, if you're making it at home, requires plenty of patience and precision. You must wait for the chicken to fully brine in the marinade, a process that can take as many as eight hours (and up to 24 if you're using the Raising Cane's method). Then, you'll have to make sure the oil is at the proper temperature; if it's too hot, for example, your chicken will likely burn on the outside before it fully cooks on the inside. With all this work going into making perfectly crispy fried chicken, you'll want the leftovers — that is, if you have any! — to sing just as beautifully in the future as the chicken did when it was fresh. And to do that, you might use the two-step reheating method, which involves your microwave and an air fryer.</p> <p>Your microwave? Really? It's true, microwaves are usually not the most desirable appliances when it comes to reheating fried chicken, but hear us out. You'll just use yours as a sort of brief preheat to start the warming process and take the chill off the meat. Try zapping it for about a minute on high — any longer, and that crispy crust you worked so hard to achieve can become tough and chewy, exactly the opposite of the light, crunchy exterior you're trying to revive.</p> <p>Then, move those drumsticks, thighs, or breasts to the air fryer for about five minutes at 375 degrees Fahrenheit to re-crisp the breading. The microwave step also keeps you from having to air fry the chicken for quite as long, which means less chance that it will burn or dry out in the second step.</p> <p>Reheating fried chicken is something of a science, but it's not a difficult discipline. You can help the process along if you take the chicken out of the fridge about half an hour before you intend to heat and eat it (just don't forget about it; it's only safe out of the icebox for up to two hours). This allows the chicken to shed even more of that refrigerator chill so that the microwave and the air fryer can do their jobs even more evenly. And be sure to place something underneath the chicken, like parchment paper, in the air fryer to avoid grease dripping to the bottom and causing smoking.</p> <p>Another way to help the fried chicken heat more evenly is to consider your microwave's science and arrange the larger pieces in a donut shape around a plate, with the smaller pieces on the inside. The chicken on the outside receives more heat in the minute that it gets zapped, but since those pieces are thicker, they can withstand it better.</p> <p>Then, when it comes to the air fryer step, it's important that you follow general meat reheating best practices and not crowd the basket. Make sure that every piece has enough space for the air to circulate all around it, with no overlapping pieces that could develop soggy spots.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2308373/leftover-fried-chicken-juicier-reheating-method/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9757"> <h2>#9757. Willo</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> A companion you talk to while you play WoW </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/willo-2?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1311043?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/willo-2" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9756"> <h2>#9756.
