Trainn MCP</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Create product videos and courses from any AI chat </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/trainn?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1313622?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/trainn" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9747"> <h2>#9747. How to clean cast iron  : It’s simpler than you think.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/How%20to%20Clean%20Cast%20Iron_Blog_2026_Shot%201_0070.jpg" alt="How to clean cast iron  : It’s simpler than you think." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Despite what you may have heard, cleaning and maintaining a cast iron skillet or Dutch oven isn’t difficult. It’s practically impossible to ruin a well-seasoned skillet, and despite your best efforts, sometimes food will stick. If your cast iron is covered in stuck-on bits of cheese from a batch of Crispy Cheesy Pan Pizza, here's how to clean it.</p> <p>We can settle the debate once and for all: Yes, you can use soap to clean your cast iron. Dishwashing soap will not damage the seasoning that makes your skillet non-stick. Polymerized oil creates the layer of seasoning through heat, and dish soap isn’t strong enough to break that bond.</p> <p>No, you cannot clean a cast iron skillet in the dishwasher. This will degrade the seasoning layer and cause it to rust.</p> <p>You should not soak a cast iron pan either; the water will cause it to rust. If you do end up rusting your pan, you can still rescue it by scrubbing off the rust then re-seasoning the pan.</p> <p>Using warm, soapy water, scrub the pan with a stiff-bristled brush or sponge to remove any food residue. Avoid harsh, abrasive scrubbers like steel wool or metal pads, which can strip the pan of its seasoning.</p> <p>Once cleaned, fully dry the pan with a kitchen towel, or place it onto a burner over low heat so the water fully evaporates. Don’t walk away from the pan — it can quickly get smoky once the water has evaporated.</p> <p>Regardless of which method you prefer, it’s imperative that the pan is fully dry. Water (not soap!) is the enemy of cast iron, which can cause it to rust. Once dry, add a few drops of neutral oil and spread all over the pan with a towel.</p> <p>Photography by Patrick Marinello; styling by Yekaterina Boytsova</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Topping inspiration for your favorite pizza</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/21/how-to-clean-cast-iron" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9746"> <h2>#9746. Forget Salmon: This Fast-Cooking Fish Has Fewer Calories</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/forget-salmon-this-fast-cooking-fish-has-fewer-calories/l-intro-1794216240.jpg" alt="Forget Salmon: This Fast-Cooking Fish Has Fewer Calories" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Salmon's rich intensity also means it generally has more calories, which can mean different things based on someone's dietary needs. If you're conscious of this and still want something that cooks up quickly (and deliciously), try flounder, a leaner, lower-calorie option that never lacks flavor.</p> <p>Exact calorie amounts can vary quite a bit, especially when it comes to wild versus farmed salmon, but even the leanest ones usually sit between 130 and 200 calories per three-ounce serving. Flounder populations, however, have a more uniform lifestyle and consistently clock in at around 100 calories per three-ounce serving. That brown or gray layer of fat may help a salmon migrate and survive cold waters, but flounder are sedentary ambush predators that don't have nearly the same energy requirements. On your plate, this means a fillet of flounder is lean, clean-tasting, and quite mild compared to a richly marbled piece of salmon.</p> <p>Because flounder is often thinner and far less fatty than salmon, that also means it cooks exponentially quicker. While a skin-on fillet can widen your margin of error, it's still much easier to render your tender fish into a dense, rubbery mess. Your best bet is to treat it like a lean steak and use a hot and fast cooking method, letting a bit of carryover cooking finish the center rather than trying to reach the perfect temperature in a pan or on the grill.</p> <p>Flounder is delicate, light, and can easily lose its natural flavor if seasoned too heavily. While it's not exactly a beginner-friendly fish, the best ways to cook it are often straightforward and focus on timing and temperature, not technique. Hands-off methods that require little manipulation or rely on a sauce for flavor are usually ideal and keep your meat moist and tender.</p> <p>If you haven't tried making a meunière yet, it's a classic seafood dish you should try at least once. Made by combining browned butter, lemon, and parsley, it's just flavorful enough to elevate your flounder without overwhelming it. Just about any French butter sauce, from beurre blanc to béchamel, is great with flounder because it adds a bit of richness and is a great vehicle for other tasty seasonings. Plus, they're flavorful enough that you'll only have to pan-sear each side of your fish, reducing the chance that it'll fall apart or overcook.</p> <p>Flounder grows more delicate the more it's cooked, so preparation methods that rely on you only handling it when raw are also quite ideal. Baking is a precise method, and you only have to move the fish once to transfer it to a plate. On the other hand, flounder is fantastic when deep-fried, and the breading helps it hold its shape. You'll still want to use a large, slotted tool and a delicate hand when fishing it out, but all you need to do is batter and drop it into oil for a great result.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2310441/forget-salmon-fast-cooking-fish-fewer-calories-flounder/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9744"> <h2>#9744. For More Flavorful Fried Eggs, Add A Teaspoon Of This Spicy Ingredient To The Pan</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/for-more-flavorful-fried-eggs-add-a-teaspoon-of-this-spicy-ingredient-to-the-pan/l-intro-1794295496.jpg" alt="For More Flavorful Fried Eggs, Add A Teaspoon Of This Spicy Ingredient To The Pan" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.</p> <p>Know the right fried egg cooking hacks, and your breakfast can easily take on a gourmet twist. For one such easy enhancement, try a hit of spice — just a teaspoon of harissa will effectively flavor eggs. Hailing from Tunisia, this smoky-savory condiment consists of chilies, garlic, and a wide assortment of spices (often cumin and coriander), all blended into a smooth dark-red consistency. It's a bold but not overwhelming blend of flavors that shines alongside eggs in a pan.</p> <p>For the greatest ease amidst bleary-eyed mornings, you can buy the spice online in the form of paste in a jar or tube. Don't confuse the condiment with powdered harissa seasoning, a dry blend with a similar flavor profile, but not the right composition for this application — though it might do very well mixed into scrambled eggs.</p> <p>Instead, you'll want a whole teaspoon of the paste itself. Heat up the pan, and throw it into a hot neutral oil, creating an aromatic red bath of chilis and spices. Follow this up by cracking in a fried egg or two, and sizzle up the lot in the fragrant oil. You'll get eggs with a dark red color and a warm dose of spice, making a dish with a lot of flavor yet not much fuss.</p> <p>Fried eggs make for a wondrously versatile food, fit as both a dish garnish and a meal in themselves. Upgraded with an ingredient like harissa, such versatile applications continue — only now with a bold hit of spice. You can integrate the seasoned eggs into a wide array of dishes.</p> <p>Start by taking inspiration from çilbir, a Turkish egg dish consisting of poached eggs, pepper-spiced butter, and yogurt. Consider serving the harissa fried eggs atop a thick and tangy dairy canvas, like Greek-style yogurt or salty labneh. Scooped up with bread or pita, it's a satisfying meal that doesn't require much effort. You can also make a quick and easy shakshuka-style fried egg by creating a base of tomato paste and harissa for your eggs to simmer in.</p> <p>Once lunch or dinner rolls around, add a little heft to the dish. Harissa-spiced eggs make for a great topping atop extra crunchy chickpeas or a creamy batch of white beans. A pork chop topped with a fried egg is a tried-and-true classic, and the harissa element will lend the construction an extra touch of spice. Not to mention, fried eggs belong atop sauteed greens, too; it's a terrific enhancement to a bowl of kale, for example. Harissa-spiced eggs deliver an aromatic punch, making them a culinary combo worth keeping in mind.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2311804/more-flavorful-fried-eggs-spicy-ingredient-pan-harissa/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9740"> <h2>#9740. Kairos</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Personal analytics engine across health, finances, & social </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/kairos-18?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1307926?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/kairos-18" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9739"> <h2>#9739. How to proof bread in the oven: Common challenge, simple solution.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-09/how%20to%20proof%20bread%20in%20oven.jpg" alt="How to proof bread in the oven: Common challenge, simple solution." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>During proofing, bread and other yeasted doughs do best in a temperature-controlled, humid, draft-free environment. Your kitchen counter may not cut it (especially in colder months), but is there a corner of your kitchen that fits that description? Yes, your oven — and you don’t even need to fire it up!</p> <p>Yeast dough is happiest when rising at temperatures between 75°F and 78°F. It will certainly rise in cooler or warmer temperatures. But for most doughs, that range is optimum for both yeast development and bread flavor.</p> <p>Your oven’s interior will pretty much mirror room temperature. And depending on the time of year (or how much you use air conditioning), that temperature could be pretty cool—too cool for yeast’s comfort.</p> <p>To get the oven up to that ideal proofing temperature, people often turn to a couple of different methods. I decided to try a bunch of them to see which is best — and helpfully, there was a clear winner.</p> <p>It’s tempting to simply preheat the oven for a minute or so to warm its interior; but not only is this hit-and-miss (How long should I leave it on? Will the oven get too hot?), it’s ineffective; the heat quickly dissipates once you turn the oven off.</p> <p>Enter your oven light. When turned on, your oven light’s slow, gentle heat will gradually warm the oven to the desired temperature. After trying a number of different methods for proofing bread in the oven, including several listed below, this was my clear favorite because it created the ideal temperature (not too hot, not too cold), maintained that temperature for several hours, and was essentially failproof (no overshooting the temp, for example!).</p> <p>It can take your oven a while to reach the desired temperature, especially if your kitchen is cold to begin with. With so many variables — season, climate, kitchen, oven — you’ll want to do a simple experiment to determine your own best method for turning your oven into an effective, efficient proof box:</p> <p>Take your oven’s temperature before turning on the light. Then turn on the light and measure the temperature again at 15-minute intervals, to see just how quickly the light warms things up. For reference, the light in my electric oven takes about an hour to raise the oven’s interior temperature by 10 degrees, and another hour to raise it an additional five degrees; your results will probably vary a bit.</p> <p>Warm your oven to about 80°F before turning off the light. Over the next couple of hours, the temperature will gradually drift down by about 10 degrees, giving your rising dough plenty of time in and around that 75°F to 78°F sweet spot.</p> <p>Once you know how to warm your oven using only its lightbulb, think about maintaining humidity: Dry dough can develop a tough skin, which inhibits rising.</p> <p>If you’re proofing dough in a bowl (or later, a shaped loaf in a pan), cover it with a clear plastic shower cap or reusable plastic bowl cover. Whatever you use, make sure it's large enough to form a “poof” on top, so the cover doesn’t touch the rising dough.</p> <p>For shaped rolls (or anything else in a large, flat pan), use an extra-large shower cap; or simply drape the pan with well-greased plastic wrap, waxed paper, or parchment.</p> <p>What if your oven doesn’t have a light, the lightbulb only lights when you open the oven door, or it’s a “cool” LED bulb?</p> <p>Then your best bet is a pan of boiling water set on the lowest rack, which will both warm and humidify your oven’s interior. Place the bread dough on the oven’s middle rack; no need to cover it.  Set a shallow pan (e.g., 9" x 13" pan) on the lower rack, and add four cups of boiling water. Quickly close the oven door.</p> <p>Your oven’s temperature will immediately rise by about 30 degrees, which will probably be warmer than you want. Cool it down by opening the door wide for about five minutes; the temperature should drop about 15 degrees.</p> <p>As the water in the oven cools, the air around it cools, too. But it happens so gradually that your oven should still remain sufficiently warm for the one to two hours your bread typically needs to rise. For longer-rising breads, simply switch out the cool water with another pan of hot water, if necessary.</p> <p>Some ovens actually have a proof setting or proofing drawer. I don’t always love using this setting, though: Most are programmed to temperatures ranging from 90°F to 100°F, far warmer than yeast dough’s optimal 75°F to 78°F. For best results, figure out how long it takes to reach about 80°F, then turn it off.</p> <p>Tip #1: If you have to open the oven door to check your rising dough, don’t worry. Unlike the huge 15- to 20-degree drop you experience when opening a fully heated oven, the temperature inside your light- or steam-warmed oven will only drop by a degree or two.</p> <p>Tip #2: Typically, you don’t preheat your oven with rising dough inside. So when your dough is close to fully risen, remove it from the oven and set it somewhere safe. (If there’s room, the top of your fridge is both warm and out of harm’s way.) Timed just right, your bread will be perfectly proved by the time the oven finishes preheating.</p> <p>Tip #3: To prevent someone from killing your rising dough by turning on the oven (say, to warm their leftover pizza), write “NO!” on a sticky note and affix it to the oven’s start button. Really!</p> <p>For the highly passionate bread baker (or a small baking business), an electronic proof box like the Brod & Taylor Proofer Pro is a step up from proofing dough in the oven. It controls temperature with exquisite precision, from cold-proofing (down to 41°F) for those overnight ferments up to 122°F for an express warmup, all while ensuring perfect humidity. Wi-Fi and programmable timers let you control your dough’s development for up to eight days. It’s literally set it and forget it — the process is simple, but the results are simply amazing.</p> <p>Still looking for a warm, draft-free spot for your rising bread dough? Think beyond your oven to other major appliances: Both your clothes dryer and dishwasher can double as a proof box!</p> <p>Cover photo by Mark Weinberg; food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Dough temperature is key to achieving consistently great results in your bread baking.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/23/how-to-proof-bread-in-oven" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9738"> <h2>#9738. Filament by Galaxy</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Move data using your terminal or agent. Fast & open source. </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/galaxy?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1282575?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/galaxy" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9737"> <h2>#9737. 9 Best Budget Olive Oils, According To Home Cooks</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/9-best-budget-olive-oils-according-to-home-cooks/l-intro-1794317707.jpg" alt="9 Best Budget Olive Oils, According To Home Cooks" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Olive oil is a highly coveted ingredient due to its rich flavor, versatility, and numerous health benefits. While the price of some olive oils — such as the $50 per bottle olive oil Martha Stewart stands by — might have you convinced this golden liquid is too pricey for your wallet, the truth is that's simply not the case. Home cooks know this precious oil doesn't have to cost an arm and a leg. While they may hold no accolades or Michelin stars, household cooks carry a wealth of knowledge when it comes to which olive oils are best for daily use.</p> <p>There are plenty of sensational olive oils found at affordable prices, from the mild and mellow-tasting to robust EVOOs bursting with grassy and fruity notes. Whether you're on the hunt for single-sourced EVOO or cold-pressed olive oil, there are plenty of budget-friendly options out there that don't compromise on quality. From those ideal for cooking with to those that add the perfect burst of flavor to finish a dish, it's time to reveal the olive oils that have earned heaps of praise from average home cooks like you and me.</p> <p>Prices are as of the date of publication and may vary based on region.</p> <p>Any culinary enthusiast looking to buy extra virgin olive oil in bulk should consider Costco's house brand for a great value cooking oil. Kirkland offers an assortment of budget-friendly olive oils in two and three liter bottles, ensuring home cooks won't be running out of this precious liquid anytime soon.</p> <p>Kirkland's Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil is particularly prized by home cooks, with supporters calling its aroma elegant and its flavor distinctive and rich. Others describe it as balanced, smooth, and mild, making it ideal for those seeking a mellower cooking oil. Aspiring chefs love its light flavor and aroma, stating it's not only great for cooking, but for whipping up appetizers, like a classic bruschetta caprese. An olive oil with a pleasing color and thickness, many consider it a great choice for everyday uses given its affordable $10.50 per liter price tag.</p> <p>However, those looking for a heartier-flavored olive oil may be drawn to try Kirkland's Spanish Extra Virgin Olive Oil, which is equally praised. Those who prepare meals on the daily appreciate its more robust flavor along with the $9.50 per liter cost, making it the most cost-effective of all Kirkland's EVOO offerings. Home cooks find it to possess fruity notes with a pleasant bite. Many, in fact, prefer it over Costco's more expensive Italian EVOO.</p> <p>Trader Joe's stocks a 32-ounce bottle of Premium Extra Virgin Olive Oil for just $12.49 ($0.39 per ounce), offering up a great choice for those counting their pennies. Crafted from a blend of olives cultivated in Italy, Spain, Argentina, and Greece, this cold-pressed olive oil (a method of making olive oil that includes no heat or chemicals, which many believe creates an oil with more nutrients and health benefits) is one home cooks call great quality for the price. Supporters pronounce it to be wonderful for both cooking and finishing dishes, with one EVOO enthusiast calling it the best tasting offering on the market.</p> <p>Family chefs appreciate the noticeable aroma of this EVOO, finding it to have a nice finish with a good amount of pungency. Reviewers describe this reasonably priced olive oil as truly delicious, praising the way it cooks. Home cooks declare it to be extremely versatile, being a great choice whether you drizzle it, use it in a fryer, or wield it in a spray bottle. Fans of this budget-friendly oil also appreciate the handy attached spout, making for easy pouring from this hefty bottle.</p> <p>A bottle that always states where the olives are sourced, you know exactly what you're getting when you purchase this wallet-approved cooking oil. An olive oil that is surprisingly well priced for the amount, Trader Joe's Premium Extra Virgin Olive Oil is one that makes a good, multipurpose olive oil, perfect for the everyday.</p> <p>Are you drawn to premium olive oils, like Graza, but put off by the high price? Well Trader Joe's might have just the item for you. The internet is calling Trader Joe's Main Squeeze Extra Virgin Olive Oil a great dupe for the more expensive olive oil brand Graza. Equipped with an incredibly handy squeezable bottle, home cooks describe this olive oil as a great cooking olive oil with a nice, grassy flavor.</p> <p>Undoubtedly, part of this EVOO's appeal is the squeezable container it comes in, which makes it easier to control the amount of oil released. You'll find no messy olive oil running down the side of the bottle post-use or accidentally sloshing too much into the pan, thanks to its adjustable top. Upon purchasing Trader Joe's Main Squeeze Extra Virgin Olive Oil, one home cook notes that this enjoyable olive oil will have you convinced you need to be splashing it on everything, from pizza crusts to pasta and soups. But, the reusable container this EVOO comes in is not its only draw.</p> <p>This olive oil is cold-pressed, imported from the Mediterranean, and can be delightfully drizzled over everything, from roasted veggies to burrata. Available in a sizable 25.4-ounce bottle for $10.99, this Mediterranean EVOO clocks in at an affordable $0.43 per ounce. Compared to Graza's olive oils, which average around $21 for a similar product, this makes it an alluring buy indeed.</p> <p>Found in affordable two packs and three packs at Costco, Terra Delyssa continues to be a budget-conscious olive oil beloved by many home cooks. A single-source olive oil crafted from Tunisian olives, one fan describes Terra Delyssa Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil as smooth and herbaceous, never holding any bitter notes, making it perfect for pan-frying and salad dressings.</p> <p>Currently offered for $34.99 for a 3-pack of 25.5-ounce bottles at Costco, this EVOO comes out to an enticing $0.46 per ounce. Home cooks love it for three simple reasons: It comes in a glass bottle, boasts a single country origin, and it tastes good. Household cooks praise this high-quality olive oil for its unique and versatile quality, stating it elevates the flavor of any dish you add it to.</p> <p>The fact that it's non-GMO and USDA organic doesn't hurt either. Even more intriguing, the olives used in Terra Delyssa Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil are pesticide-free, harvested by hand, and cold-pressed within four hours of picking. The result is an olive oil abundant in antioxidants, low in acidity, and high in polyphenol content. People also love the traceable nature of this EVOO. A quick scan of the QR code on the label lets you trace the story of your olive oil from the orchard to the bottle.</p> <p>Anyone looking for a single-source olive oil that won't drain their bank account should check out Trader Giotto's Sicilian Selezione Olive Oil. A product we rated the highest in our ranking of Trader Joe's best olive oils, this EVOO is truly one that stands above the rest. Its flavor is exceptionally smooth, with delectable fruity notes and a pronounced peppery end note to round it out. Better yet, this golden elixir costs a meagre $10.99 per 16.9-ounce bottle, amounting to about $0.65 per ounce.</p> <p>A bottle that is astoundingly affordable for a single-source EVOO, this noteworthy olive oil is rendered from olives that are grown, picked, and pressed on Italy's island of Sicily. The final flavor? An olive oil that has a light, peppery finish that tingles the throat — a signature of high-quality extra virgin olive oil. This tingling sensation is due to oleocanthal, a compound that causes a slight burn in the back of the throat, and a sign that the olive oil is fresh and pure.</p> <p>An EVOO that Consumer Reports also rated as one of the best extra virgin olive oils at Trader Joe's, this is a great choice for those looking for a product that won't go bad before you have a chance to use it up. While you can certainly cook with this olive oil, home cooks find this to be an ideal choice for finishing dishes.</p> <p>Those looking for a premium olive oil at a wallet-friendly price will be drawn to Aldi's Specially Selected Sicilian Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Weighing in at $12.35 for a 16.9-ounce bottle ($0.73 per ounce), this Aldi exclusive might be higher priced than other Aldi options, but it's actually quite the steal given its high praise.</p> <p>An Aldi exclusive olive oil that has rightfully earned a place in your shopping cart, home cooks herald this olive oil for being single-sourced, with all ingredients originating in Italy. Other culinary enthusiasts applaud this EVOO for its striking hue and hearty flavor, labeling the taste as subtly grassy. Many appreciate the dark glass bottle as well — a characteristic that helps protect this precious liquid from light, which can quicken spoilage and cause the oil to lose its robust flavor. If that isn't enough, this esteemed EVOO also bears a seal from Val Di Mazara P.D.O., signifying the specific region it comes from, in addition to approval from the North American Olive Oil Association, denoting its superior caliber.</p> <p>This Italian olive oil is one home cooks declare to be perfect for drizzling over just about everything from salad to pizza, as well as making a delicious olive oil cake. No wonder it took the number one spot in our ranking of Aldi olive oils.</p> <p>California Olive Ranch is a fan favorite among many home cooks.A brand that provides a range of products, from single-source 100% California olive oil to global blends, you'll find an olive oil to fit every price range here. Chefs eagerly praise California Olive Ranch EVOO for its standout flavor, declaring it to be great for a number of uses, from cooking and dipping to marinades and rubs.</p> <p>This cost-effective EVOO is priced at an inviting $13 to $17 for a 16.9-ounce bottle of the global blends, which are offered in mild, medium, and robust varieties. It's an olive oil home cooks find to be surprisingly affordable compared to other better-known brands. The medium global blend in particular strikes a crowd-pleasing middle ground, securing the perfect balance between peppery and mild while still holding a classic grassy characteristic.</p> <p>Still, if you're looking for more of a finishing oil, the 100% California might be more appealing. Devotees of this single-source, California-exclusive olive oil declare it to be well-rounded, mild-tasting, and incredibly delicious, making it a great choice for just about everything from marinades and sautéing to baking delectable desserts. Additionally, culinary enthusiasts love the dark, glass bottle this EVOO comes in, along with the non-GMO project verification and vegan certification. Priced around $18 to $20 for a 16.9-ounce bottle, it may be more expensive, but it's an olive oil home cooks claim to last a while.</p> <p>A preferred brand of chef Giada De Laurentiis, Lucini is a store-bought olive oil admired by many households for its flavor and versatility. Lucini Everyday Extra Virgin Olive Oil can be found at a reasonable $13.49 per 16.9-ounce bottle (about $0.80 per ounce), rendering it a pretty affordable option compared to higher end brands. One Amazon reviewer declared this EVOO to "be a steal" compared to what is being sold elsewhere in the U.S., calling the taste amazing and the price truly unbeatable.</p> <p>EVOO fans find the cost to be fitting for the quality, declaring you can definitely taste the caliber when dipping bread into this delightful EVOO. Just add a little salt and pepper, and this palatable olive oil will do the rest. One supporter preferred it over Lucini's premium olive oil, claiming the Lucini Everyday Extra Virgin Olive Oil to possess a stronger bite, with more peppery and complex notes.</p> <p>However, Lucini's Premium Select Extra Virgin Olive Oil has its backers as well. A single-source Italian oil, home cooks commend this cold-pressed EVOO for its smell, perfect for use in all applications, from cooking to salad dressings. They find the bottle perfectly sized, ensuring you use up the contents before it loses its quality. Priced at $23.99 for a 16.9-ounce bottle, it may be slightly pricier, but it's an olive oil well worth considering for its rich, buttery flavor and pungent finish.</p> <p>Many are shocked at the affordable price of BONO Sicilian Val Di Mazara PDO Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil, given its similarity to higher-end brands in taste. With a flavor one Redditor described as "pleasantly bitter and grassy, with a rich mouthfeel," many are astounded by this EVOO's phenomenal flavor profile. One avid supporter named it the best olive oil they had ever tried, finding it devoid of any bitterness at all.</p> <p>Domestic cooks admire this non-GMO project verified, USDA organic certified EVOO, loving the gorgeous yellow color and authentic Italian flavors. Upon sampling, one olive oil enthusiast declared the taste to transport them back to Italy, conjuring images of dining upon mozzarella and fresh tomatoes drizzled with olive oil. Another supporter lauded the vibrant aroma and well-balanced flavor, professing it to contain the perfect ratio of peppery flavor and smoothness, which ends in a pleasantly buttery finish.</p> <p>While more expensive than other household brands, its $24.99 price tag for a 16.9-ounce bottle is pretty exceptional considering the Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) certified status of this single-source olive oil, which ensures the olives that make up this delectable liquid come solely from the Val Di Mazara region of Italy. The process is supervised from growth to harvest and processing, undergoing rigorous testing to confirm the quality before being granted a one-of-a-kind serial number, denoting its authenticity and lineage.</p> <p>To select the best budget olive oils recommended by home cooks, we assessed a number of online reviews, discussions, and social media posts by household cooks and amateur chefs. From here, we selected the most notable olive oils to be found at affordable prices, seeking out the best value oils that still held high-quality characteristics, such as cold-pressing, organic ingredients, or simply an exceptional taste. A range of olive oils were included in this article, from wallet-friendly options that are ideal for cooking and baking with to those that are best for raw uses and finishing dishes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2311069/best-budget-olive-oils-according-home-cooks/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9736"> <h2>#9736. Couples Who Do This Together Have Stronger Marriages (M)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/couple-2-6.jpg" alt="Couples Who Do This Together Have Stronger Marriages (M)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>One simple shared activity may help couples communicate better and strengthen their marriage.</p> <p>One simple shared activity may help couples communicate better and strengthen their marriage.</p> <p>• Read members-only articles • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. The Traditional Kitchen Knife Bobby Flay Recommends Is On Amazon</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/the-traditional-kitchen-knife-bobby-flay-recommends-is-on-amazon/l-intro-1794307086.jpg" alt="The Traditional Kitchen Knife Bobby Flay Recommends Is On Amazon" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.</p> <p>Whether you're an amateur home cook or a seasoned chef, a high-quality chef's knife is one of the three knives you need in your kitchen arsenal. However, with so many options out there, choosing the right one can quickly become overwhelming. You'll want something versatile enough to finely chop vegetables, break down a chicken, and handle just about everything in between. Durability matters, too. A good knife should last for years, if not a lifetime, with the right care. And, of course, it needs to hold its sharp edge. Luckily, Food Network star Bobby Flay has a recommendation that takes some of the guesswork out of the process (per The Kitchn): the Shun Classic 8-inch Western Cook's Knife, available on Amazon.</p> <p>Before getting into the knife's many selling points, there's one thing we have to address. At $163.95 (which is the sale price — it's normally around $205), it's certainly not a budget-friendly buy. But there are plenty of reasons why we think it could be worth the investment. At its core, knife steel is a blend of iron and carbon, with manufacturers adding other elements to improve its performance. It's these added elements that set Shun knives apart from the rest.</p> <p>The Shun Classic 8-inch Western Cook's knife uses a proprietary blend called VG-MAX, which is specifically formulated to resist corrosion and wear while maintaining a sharp edge. It also has a high carbon content, helping the blade achieve the hardness needed for excellent edge retention. The combination of elements in VG-MAX gives the Shun an advantage over many more affordable knives made with lower-grade steel, which have the tendency to lose their sharpness far more quickly with regular use. In other words, you're paying for a knife that's designed to stay sharp, rather than one that needs constant maintenance to keep it performing.</p> <p>If the name didn't give it away already, Shun is a Japanese knife brand, and all its knives are handcrafted in Seki City, a region renowned for centuries of sword and knife making. Any kitchen nerd knows that Japanese knives are up there with German ones when it comes to quality, so just by looking at the place of origin, you can expect a considerable degree of craftsmanship to have gone into this blade.</p> <p>Interestingly, despite its Japanese origins, the Shun Classic 8-inch Western Cook's Knife doesn't adopt the traditional santoku shape, often considered Japan's answer to the Western chef's knife. Both blades are versatile, all-purpose kitchen knives, but they differ in their blade profiles and the way they're typically used. Neither is necessarily better than the other; that distinction largely comes down to personal preference and preferred cutting style.</p> <p>While the blade might not have a traditional Japanese shape, the handle certainly draws on Japanese craftsmanship. It's made from Pakkawood, an engineered composite created by stacking thin hardwood veneers and infusing them with phenolic resin, which is then bonded together using high heat. The result of this admittedly complicated process is a durable, moisture-resistant material that's less prone to warping and cracking than ordinary wood. This makes it easy to keep clean, although that doesn't mean you should put the knife in the dishwasher or leave it to soak in the sink. Even quality materials can't protect even the most durable blades from the harsh detergents, water, and high temperatures, which will inevitably cause rusting and damage over time. Hand-washing and drying your knife promptly remains the better option.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2311850/kitchen-knife-bobby-flay-recommends-amazon/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; The secret to make-ahead pie crust? Pie crumbs.: Get ahead on your pie baking right now.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/pie%20crumsb.jpg" alt="The secret to make-ahead pie crust? Pie crumbs.: Get ahead on your pie baking right now." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>'Tis the season — to start thinking about holiday baking. And while this time of year is full of joy and celebration, it can also be stressful. We’re all searching for ways to get ahead of the curve, and one of the easiest? Make-ahead pie crust, made using pie crumbs.</p> <p>I first learned of this technique from a 90-something friend with whom I love to talk baking. Over lunch one day, something she said about pie captured my attention.</p> <p>"Did you ever hear of pie crumbs?" she asked. I admitted I hadn't — aside from the obvious: the scraps of pie crust left on the plate after the slice is gone. "My mother used to mix flour and salt and lard together to make this crumbly mixture that she'd store in a crock in the cellar. She called them her pie crumbs. When she wanted to make a pie, she'd just scoop out a few handfuls, add water, and roll out her crust."</p> <p>Sounds like a good make-ahead solution for 100 years ago — but now that we have easy access to freezers, why not just make pie dough and freeze it in ready-to-roll disks? A couple of reasons, actually.</p> <p>1) Pie crumbs allow you to make any amount of crust, from mini apple pies to a crust for a deep-dish 10" pie. With frozen disks, you're looking at a standard single crust — not always exactly what you want.</p> <p>2) Pie crumbs save time. Remove however much of the crumbly mixture you need (more on this below) from the freezer, and within 15 minutes the fat is soft enough that you can add water and roll out your crust. Compare that to the hours it takes to thaw and roll a frozen disk of prepared crust — not to mention the elbow grease if your crust isn’t fully thawed.</p> <p>3) Pie crumbs can be more stable in the freezer than pie crust disks. Why? Because without the added water, no ice crystals form. Ice crystals can damage the flour/water matrix, leading to changes in its structure (which can then potentially lead to changes in your pie crust).</p> <p>Oh, and one other reason I like pie crumbs: If my friend's mother used them, they were probably a 19th-century kitchen time-saver. And I love the feeling of preserving and carrying forward our American baking traditions — even something as simple as a shortcut for pie crust.</p> <p>Choose a standard pie crust recipe: Our Classic Double Pie Crust recipe is good choice, but anything that involves cutting fat into flour (lard, shortening, butter, etc.) will work.</p> <p>Mix flour, salt, and shortening and/or butter: Follow your recipe up until all of the fat is incorporated into the flour. You should be left with a bowl of dry, crumbly dough that barely holds together when squeezed. If using butter, you should be able to see visible chunks scattered throughout the dough.</p> <p>Weigh the pie crumbs: If you’re making a large batch of pie crumbs, it’s helpful to weigh and label the total gram amount so that you can easily remove the amount of pie crumbs for a single pie crust as needed. Our Classic Double Pie Crust makes 488 grams of pie crumbs; that means 244 grams per single pie crust. Label these amounts on your freezer storage bag.</p> <p>Bag, label, and freeze the crumbs: Seal pie crumbs in an airtight, freezer-safe bag and place in the freezer, preferably in the back where it won't be subject to warm air wafting over it each time you open the freezer door.</p> <p>Scoop crumbs out of the bag into a bowl: Whether one crust, two crusts, or one and a half, do the math and measure the crumbs based on your recorded gram amounts.</p> <p>Let the crumbs thaw for 15 to 20 minutes or so: Wait until the butter chunks feel barely pliable in your fingers.</p> <p>Add water and mix: Add water based on your original recipe amount, or just enough water to make a chunky mass when mixed. Squeeze and knead the dough briefly; all you're doing here is bringing the chunks together into one solid piece of dough.</p> <p>Roll the dough, place in a pan, and bake accordingly: From here, your pie crust is the same as any fresh-made crust and can be filled and baked or prebaked for a no-bake filling. (Bonus: Because the crumbs were frozen and remain cold as you work with them, there's no need to chill your rolled-out crust before filling and/or baking.)</p> <p>Fairly indefinitely, though the longer they're frozen, the more chance they have both to absorb freezer odors, and for the fats to start to go off. I've also found that, after about two weeks in the freezer, I need to add a touch more water than usual to bring the dough together — due to the drying effects inherent in freezing.</p> <p>With pie season hard upon us, now's the time to try pie crumbs for make-ahead pie crust. Or maybe you have another old-fashioned pie trick up your sleeve? Share your favorite tips in the comments, below.</p> <p>For detailed ingredient amounts for the crust demonstrated above, see our recipe for Classic Double Pie Crust.</p> <p>And if you're looking for additional time-saving ways to use your freezer in the run-up to the holidays, check out our recipe for Homemade Brown and Serve Rolls and Apple Pie with Make-Ahead Filling.</p> <p>Cover photo and food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>Because we're all wondering what to do with our apple and pumpkin pies.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/26/make-ahead-pie-crust" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9731"> <h2>#9731. Google Pixel Tag</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Google’s $30 Android-ready tracking tag </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/google?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1312154?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/google" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9730"> <h2>#9730. Skip Regular Butter And Oil: Roasted Potatoes Are 10x Crispier With This Ingredient</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/skip-regular-butter-and-oil-roasted-potatoes-are-10x-crispier-with-this-ingredient/l-intro-1794238653.jpg" alt="Skip Regular Butter And Oil: Roasted Potatoes Are 10x Crispier With This Ingredient" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>A mistake everyone makes with crispy roasted potatoes is using the wrong cooking fat, which tends to burn under the high heat required for great texture. Regular butter and oil each have their strengths, but neither gets quite the same result as ghee, a type of clarified butter with Indian origins.</p> <p>High-smoke-point oil is great for roasted potatoes because it lets you use high heat to crisp the exteriors. However, it doesn't add much in the way of flavor, so you're missing out on an opportunity to layer on more depth. On the other hand, butter is great at making a hearty side dish, but the milk solids tend to burn at temperatures above 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Ghee, however, has virtually no milk solids and very little moisture, making it the perfect middle ground. With a smoke point of around 450 degrees Fahrenheit and a rich flavor, it's the perfect way to achieve great texture without sacrificing taste.</p> <p>The biggest difference between ghee and clarified butter is taste and color. The former comes "pre-toasted," giving it a deep golden hue and an intense nuttiness that essentially kick-starts the roasted flavor of your tubers. Even if you don't use the various tricks to increase surface area, your potatoes will taste like they have more crispy outsides than usual. A small amount helps them develop the perfect color, giving you a showstopping presentation that tastes great, looks amazing, and still lets you use your existing favorite recipe with only one ingredient substitution.</p> <p>Ghee's flavor is more pronounced than butter's or oil's, but it's still just as versatile. Rather than switching up seasoning, it's best to focus on how to increase the "roasted" factor of your potatoes. Increasing their surface area, ensuring they have as little surface moisture as possible, and using the correct type of pan are easy ways to improve their flavor.</p> <p>There's an easy British trick for roasted potatoes that makes them exponentially crispier: roughing up the exterior. By parboiling them, then shaking them in a colander, you transform the smooth outside into one covered in tiny little ridges and bumps. These have a far greater surface area, which means your ghee has more room to help brown the exteriors, so you end up with more crispiness than normal. Not only does this improve the flavor, but it also speeds up the roasting time since you aren't cooking a raw vegetable.</p> <p>Moisture is the enemy of crispiness and can prevent even ghee from creating a great texture. If you parboiled your potatoes, letting them steam-dry for a bit makes them easier to work with and removes excess water. If cooking them raw, it may help to pat the pieces dry first to remove excess surface moisture. Either way, a heavy-bottomed pan, preferably cast iron or stainless steel, holds more heat and can develop far better color and flavor than something that is thin, flimsy, or nonstick.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2310797/skip-butter-oil-roasted-potatoes-10x-crispier-ingredient-ghee/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9729"> <h2>#9729. Templify AI</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Powerful content editor for people who aren’t editors </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/templify?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1293281?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/templify" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9728"> <h2>#9728. A Familiar Smell That Reduces Hunger And Boosts Exercise (M)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/nose-1-1.jpg" alt="A Familiar Smell That Reduces Hunger And Boosts Exercise (M)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The scent may fool the brain into feeling satisfied — and unlock better workout performance.</p> <p>The scent may fool the brain into feeling satisfied -- and unlock better workout performance.</p> <p>• Read members-only articles • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.spring.org.uk/2026/10/chocolate-hunger.php" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9727"> <h2>#9727. 10 Protein-Packed Substitutes For Mayo In Chicken Salad</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/10-protein-packed-substitutes-for-mayo-in-chicken-salad/l-intro-1794335846.jpg" alt="10 Protein-Packed Substitutes For Mayo In Chicken Salad" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Chicken salad is like edible Americana, a comfort food that's beloved for its taste, nutrition, and versatility. You can find it in the prepared section of your local supermarket or on the menu of your favorite diner. Trying to cut down on carbohydrates? Have a scoop on a salad. Want a light and easy lunch? Have it as a club or between two pieces of toasted whole-grain bread. More importantly, though, chicken salad is like a ball of clay ready to be shaped by your taste preferences. You can take it in infinite directions: Mediterranean, Southwest, Spanish, French, Indian, Vietnamese. Have some extra sprigs of cilantro or half a bag of red grapes lying hanging around the fridge? Add 'em. Don't know what to do with those leftover pecans or knob of fresh ginger? You can throw those in, too.</p> <p>But the foundation of any respectable chicken salad is its creamy binder. In that regard, mayonnaise is the undisputed classic, turning your basic diced chicken breast into something moist, savory, and luscious. However, plenty of other ingredients deliver that signature smoothness — just with more protein. From tzatziki to silken tofu to labneh, there are tons of options that deliver both texture and an added pop of flavor. Whether you're minding your macros or just looking for a new spin on a classic dish, this list of protein-packed mayo substitutes is for you.</p> <p>Yogurt has a long and storied reputation as a health food, so long, in fact, that its beneficial properties are documented in Indian Ayurvedic medicinal writings from more than 7,000 years ago. Today, it's seen as a better-for-you breakfast option, loaded with beneficial probiotics, calcium, and, of course, protein. Yogurt, especially the more thoroughly strained Greek variety, has an excellent calorie-to-protein ratio (about 16 grams of protein per 150 calories when made with whole milk), which is why it has become so popular with bodybuilders and wellness influencers.</p> <p>However, Greek yogurt still has a place in ordinary kitchens, and it's especially useful for people looking for a healthier alternative to mayonnaise, cream cheese, or any other creamy, high-fat, high-cholesterol product, which is why it makes such a great addition to homemade chicken salad. Even when prepared with mayonnaise, chicken salad is a relatively nutritious lunch option, typically made with low-fat chicken breast, fresh herbs, diced veggies, and maybe some nuts or sliced grapes. Whole milk yogurt, which is creamier than low-fat options, builds on that by adding extra protein, moisture, and the richness synonymous with a good chicken salad. It also adds a little tang that complements the subdued nature of poultry and plays well with other common chicken-salad additions, like mustard, dill, or curry powder.</p> <p>It feels like every week there's another article or study being published identifying the benefits of gut health. This increased focus on the gut microbiome and the trillions of microorganisms that occupy it has brought all sorts of fermented dairy products, which are packed with probiotics and other useful bacteria, back into the nutritional spotlight. In this department, Greek yogurt is king (at least in the United States), but other styles are slowly making their way to the supermarket dairy aisle. One of them is skyr, also known as Icelandic yogurt.</p> <p>Technically classified as a cheese because its proteins are coagulated with rennet (a naturally occurring enzyme), skyr is dense, almost custard-like, with a mild sweetness and less assertive bite than Greek yogurt. Nutritionally, the two dairy products have an almost identical profile, although skyr is typically slightly higher in protein per serving due to a more rigorous straining process. But it's that straining — and subsequent thicker texture — that makes skyr such a terrific mayo substitute, delivering the same full creaminess without the more forward lactic tang of typical yogurt. How you use it in your chicken salad is a personal preference. If you like your chicken salad on the more unctuous side, use it as is; if you like it a little looser, thin your skyr with a tablespoon or two of milk, which may also help coat each ingredient more evenly.</p> <p>On a per-calorie basis, cottage cheese is hard to beat among high-protein foods, with (on average) 12-14 grams of protein per 100-calorie serving. Unlike yogurt, which is fermented with bacteria, cottage cheese is made through acidification. As milk becomes more acidic and the pH level drops, the proteins denature, clump, and coagulate into tiny little curds. Although the process is simple, there's a lot of variability between brands. Some are saltier or creamier or contain larger curds.</p> <p>But the most influential factor, especially regarding your chicken salad, is the fat content. While low-fat cottage cheese has fewer calories per serving, it lacks the richness needed to rehydrate dry chicken. Beyond extra unctuousness, full-fat cottage cheese adds salinity, clean milky notes, and a very mild cheese flavor. However, there's one major difference between cottage cheese and mayonnaise: Texture. Straight out of the plastic tub, cottage cheese can be, well, lumpy. This may not bother you in the slightest, but if it does, there's an easy workaround: Whipping the cottage cheese. You can do this with a hand mixer, mini food processor, or even just a big fork; the goal being to break those curds into a finer texture similar to ricotta. You can use the same technique to incorporate this high-protein food into smoothies, dips, and even macaroni and cheese.</p> <p>Hummus was the "it" food product of the early 2000s, but in the years since, it has faded in popularity. Maybe we were just given too much, too fast: Beet hummus, carrot hummus, lentil hummus, chocolate hummus — each variation obfuscating the beauty of this simple, timeless, life-sustaining food. Hummus, the type made from chickpeas, sesame paste (tahini), and olive oil, is an ancient form of plant-based protein foundational to Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines. When blended, the ingredients make a velvety emulsion that — depending on how much ice water or oil you use — can be spread or scooped over everything, from bulgur wheat to falafel wraps.</p> <p>It's also a great addition to salads — including ones made from chicken. Here, hummus provides an extra protein boost as well as some much-needed fattiness. Its blend of Middle Eastern spices — cumin, sumac, garlic, za'atar — contributes a warmth and brightness that cuts through the inherent blandness of cooked chicken breast. If using hummus as the foundation of your chicken salad, consider adding other Mediterranean ingredients, like capers, olives, walnuts, almonds, fresh tomato, or cucumbers. You can use your favorite supermarket brand, or just quickly whip up delicious hummus at home.</p> <p>Probably the most underrated ingredient on this list, silken tofu is a centuries-old, plant-based protein with limitless applications. Like other forms of bean curd, silken tofu is made from soybeans, but it's worlds different from soft, medium, or firm varieties. While it comes in similar packaging, silken tofu is hardly solid; it's more like a pudding or flan that will fall apart if you try to pick it up with a fork. However, it's precisely this loose creaminess that makes silken tofu such a terrific substitute for mayonnaise in your next chicken salad.</p> <p>Besides being a great protein source — containing around 20 grams per 16-ounce package — silken tofu can easily be made smooth and pourable. When blended, it becomes something akin to Alfredo sauce, with a velvety consistency that's ideal for coating chicken. Another advantage of silken tofu is its taste — or lack thereof. You're dealing with a blank canvas here, one that will quickly absorb whatever seasonings, herbs, or sauces you mix with it. It may need some doctoring to get the texture right, but just use this as another opportunity to add flavor. Try adding cilantro and lime, tarragon and sherry vinegar, or hot sauce, for a Buffalo wing-inspired chicken salad.</p> <p>There are only so many ways to add creaminess to food without relying on dairy, a fatty emulsion, or some complicated form of food chemistry. Adding a can of blended beans is one of them. Legumes, like black beans, kidney beans, and butter beans, have a starchy center that turns smooth and pillowy when blended. Most commercial varieties you find at your typical supermarket are good for cooking, but some have a more distinct flavor than others.</p> <p>When making chicken salad, it's best to use beans with a clean, neat taste and not too much earthiness. For this, white, cannellini, or Great Northern beans are best. They won't overwhelm the other ingredients in your chicken salad, but they also aren't entirely neutral-tasting, either. The key to using these legumes is to purée them with different spices, herbs, and condiments, like Worcestershire sauce, miso, or a splash of vinegar. To achieve a texture that's similar to mayonnaise, you'll likely need to add some liquid or fat. Olive or another neutral oil works, but adding a heavily seasoned broth will give you an even better result. To do this, make a quick pan sauce with sautéed aromatics, seasonings, and stock; add it to your beans, then blend everything in a blender or food processor.</p> <p>This one is a little sneaky. Egg yolks are inherently fatty, but they also contain natural emulsifiers that turn into a creamy paste when blended. That means you don't have to add a drop of mayonnaise (which, ironically, is made predominantly from egg yolks) to achieve a luscious texture. But egg salad brings more to the party than just creaminess. If you've ever watched a TikTok nutritionist worth their creatine, then you're probably frustratingly aware that egg whites are one of nature's purest protein sources.</p> <p>This combination of smooth, fatty yolk and protein-rich white makes egg salad an incredible substitute for mayo. It's a tongue-in-cheek pairing, for sure, but this whimsical culinary mashup also delivers on taste. Because eggs are a tad sulfurous on their own, season them generously with ingredients like Dijon mustard, capers, lemon juice, smoked paprika, or even a few shakes of curry powder. However, the key to achieving a natural creaminess is proper egg cookery, which essentially boils down to not overcooking your hard-boiled eggs. The answer: A quick dunk in the ice bath for about 10-15 minutes to halt cooking and preserve those fluffy yolks.</p> <p>Want the nutritional upside of yogurt with an added burst of refreshing Mediterranean flavors? Sounds like it's tzatziki time. The yogurt-based dip is most closely associated with Greek cuisine, serving as a cooling counterpoint to robustly seasoned grilled meats, fried zucchini, and platters of pita. And, while its protein content isn't on the same level as skyr or cottage cheese, it isn't negligible, either, which is why it's another smart mayo substitute for your next chicken salad.</p> <p>Tzatziki looks simple, but it delivers a chorus of complex flavors that few condiments can match. It's all things smooth, rich, tangy, and fresh, thanks to a blend of fresh herbs and other aromatics. Besides yogurt, the predominant ingredient is cucumber. Paired with fresh mint, dill, and garlic, this creates a clean, powerful taste profile. It instantly elevates ordinary chicken into something moist and tender. Slip your tzatziki-coated chicken salad into a pita and top with shredded lettuce, tomato, black olives, and sliced red onion for a memorable lunch. While tzatziki is popular, it can be difficult to find good options in your average supermarket. Thankfully, a quality tzatziki sauce is easy to put together; just remember to squeeze the moisture out of your cucumbers. Otherwise, your sauce will be too wet and separate.</p> <p>Labneh is made by straining Greek yogurt in cheesecloth until you remove the remaining liquid whey. This not only creates a denser product, but it also concentrates the flavor. It's traditionally made with goat's milk, which is a little grassy on the palate and has a slightly tangier finish than a cow's milk cheese or yogurt. Unlike yogurt, though, which you typically eat with a spoon, labneh is more of a dip, perfect for crudités, pita, lavash, or even grilled fruits. It has a decadent mouthfeel and is decidedly more savory, especially when dressed with olive oil, making it a nice way to rejuvenate an otherwise tired chicken salad.</p> <p>But there's no reason to pigeonhole this spreadable yogurt as savory or sweet; it works beautifully with both taste profiles. You can roll it in za'atar, sumac, and fresh mint, or crust it with pistachios and drizzle it with honey. Since it's the thickest yogurt-based product on this list, when using it for chicken salad, you'll likely want to add a splash of milk or a non-dairy alternative to loosen it up. If you can't find labneh in stores, you can literally just add Greek yogurt to a cheesecloth, hang it above your sink, and let it drip for a few hours until it's firm and extra creamy.</p> <p>Like most dairy products, feta is a solid protein source, with about 4 grams per 2-ounce serving; however, it differs from other cheeses because it's brined in a salt-water and whey solution rather than traditionally aged. This process helps preserve the cheese while also imbuing it with its signature salinity. If you've been lucky enough to try quality feta, you know that this soft, crumbly cheese packs a punch. In the mouth, it has a clean, fresh cream flavor and mild tang, making it a natural partner for grilled meats like beef, lamb, or chicken.</p> <p>Feta isn't spreadable, nor does it melt, but you can easily transform its texture by dropping a few chunks into a blender or food processor and "whipping" it until smooth. The result is smooth, salty, and spoonable — and perfect for chicken salad. When using whipped feta, consider both its salt content and mild acidic bite. These are strong flavors that should be balanced with other sweet and savory ingredients. Try pairing it with starchy, nutty, or mildly sweet foods like roasted butternut squash, pistachios, dried cranberries, or nectarines.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2312434/protein-packed-substitutes-mayo-in-chicken-salad/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9726"> <h2>#9726.
