How Your Imagination Can Work for You or Against You</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://ggsc.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/assets/images/how_imagination_works_in_the_brain_-_abcdef_-_0a21b39134b316e51cdc0dd96c5e6bca3c0093e9-fb_-_abcdef_-_94b15742ccdfc3b16fb1fe35872167fe8d42c35d.jpg" alt="How Your Imagination Can Work for You or Against You" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Become a subscribing member today. Help us continue to bring “the science of a meaningful life” to you and to millions around the globe.</p> <p>Greater Good Science Center • Magazine • In Action • In Education</p> <p>I have a pretty vivid imagination, sometimes for the good, sometimes not. I love it when it helps me to create new stories or songs, or when I can daydream about fun times ahead. But it can also lead to fear or worry, like when I imagine something terrible befalling the people or places I love.</p> <p>Is there some way to nurture the positive aspects of imagination while minimizing the problematic? According to Cassandra Vieten, director of research at the Arthur C. Clarke Center for Human Imagination, there is. In her new book, Imagine That, she explains imagination’s importance in our everyday lives—a way to understand our past, navigate the present, and explore future possibilities. If we learn more about its inner workings, she argues, we can use it more consciously and deliberately to create the kind of life we want.</p> <p>“Imagination is something we all possess, something we can all practice, for free and with equal opportunity,” says Vieten. “When someone develops this capacity, they gain something almost magical: the ability to see multiple futures simultaneously and navigate toward the preferred ones.”</p> <p>Many of us tend to conflate imagination with creativity, thinking that being able to imagine new ideas is the same as bringing them to fruition. While the two may indeed be related, this is far too limited a view of what imagination can be, writes Vieten.</p> <p>“Imagination is an essential, foundational capacity that allows us to simulate reality and transcend it to explore possibilities beyond the known,” she says.</p> <p>In our everyday lives, imagination is what helps us make predictions as well as come up with novel (or creative) ideas. For example, we might imagine how stopping for a coffee on our way to work will help us focus (simulation imagination, based on past experience). But we might also use our imagination to transcend what’s known and come up with a totally new innovation or product idea once we arrive at the office (generative imagination).</p> <p>“Imagination weaves throughout the fabric of our cognitive, sensory, and relational lives—you are constantly speculating, visualizing, rehearsing, wondering,” she writes.</p> <p>These types of imagination show up differently in the brain, writes Vieten. Simulation is primarily centered in the default mode network (DMN), a part of the brain that remains active when we aren’t engaging in a specific task. The DMN is where we tend to mull over future interactions, plans, or options, often subconsciously (or even unconsciously).</p> <p>Generative imagination, on the other hand, comes by freeing ourselves from the DMN’s limitations (or, some would say, tyranny). If we can get out of the everyday chatter and let our minds truly wander freely around disparate parts of the brain, making new neural connections, we have a better chance of generating something truly unique.</p> <p>“Rather than simulating or iterating, comparing and contrasting, generative imagination is focused on combining, reconfiguring, or transcending existing knowledge to generate novel outputs,” writes Vieten.</p> <p>Either way, imagination isn’t frivolous, she writes; it’s important for our everyday functioning as well as creative self-expression. It helps us solve problems, while also expanding possibilities of what could be, giving us “the gift of wonder, whimsy, and surprise, the whoas and the wows of our lives,” she writes.</p> <p>Imagination can sometimes be problematic, though. For example, we might imagine that our spouse is mad at us and worry about what might happen when she gets home from work when, actually, she’s not mad at all. This can cause us needless worry, not to mention potentially trigger a fight.</p> <p>We can also imagine that other people are unpleasant or even dangerous based on untested biases. These can be formed in part via our imagination, which tries to prepare us for unknown encounters, often behind the scenes at an unconscious level.</p> <p>“We regularly imagine entire narratives, scenes, and interactions without intending to or even knowing we’re doing it,” writes Vieten.</p> <p>Our imagination is often busy filling in the missing parts of our memories and perceptions, which are by nature incomplete. Memories, rather than being etched in our minds, are recreated (and often changed) each time they’re recalled. Similarly, we can’t perceive everything at once, so our imagination completes the picture for us, adding interpretations, too. This means it’s easy to corrupt memories or miss details of a situation—which can sometimes lead to problems (think eyewitness accounts of crimes, for example).</p> <p>Understanding these darker sides of imagination can help us tame them somewhat, says Vieten. “You can practice bringing greater attention to what you are imagining, recognize it as imagination, and decide whether it holds useful information, is irrelevant, or is actually causing harm.”</p> <p>While the book covers the neuroscience behind imagination, it’s also about how to harness our imagination more effectively. Your personal imagination style may depend, in part, on your genetics (such as neurodiversity), culture, and life experiences. Understanding this can help you figure out where you might want to try moving the needle one way or the other.</p> <p>To assess your own imaginative strengths and weaknesses, here are some key imagination modes Vieten outlines in her book.</p> <p>1. Receptiveness. “How willing you are to imagine—and how receptive you are to whatever bubbles up.” If you are high in receptivity, you may find it easy to do guided visualizations, for example; if low in receptivity, you may be less willing to imagine unknown scenarios.</p> <p>2. Presence. How much do you embody your imagined experiences? If you tend to be absorbed, immersed, and emotionally involved in imagined scenarios, you’re high in presence; if you tend to observe these imaginings from a distance, you’re less so.</p> <p>3. Embellishment. “How vivid, detailed, and elaborate people make their imaginings.” Those high in embellishment can imagine intricate scenarios with much more detail, clarity, nuance, and complexity. Those low in embellishment might be more “big picture” folks, who may not be able to conjure up details as much.</p> <p>4. Originality. How much your imagination is fueled by what is or could be, based on reality, versus how much it veers from that and is based more on fantasy and novelty.</p> <p>5. Temporality. How much your imagination is associated with time (in other words, assessing the past or projecting into the future) versus how much it is agnostic around time (not based on any particular time). (Vieten admits the science on this mode is not completely settled, but says there appear to be some differences in how people engage with time while imagining.)</p> <p>Each of these modes has pros and cons, she argues. For example, being high in receptivity may mean you’re more cognitively flexible and open to new experiences, but can also mean you’re overly compliant and easily manipulated. Similarly, the upside of being high in originality is that it can fuel advancements in art and science, though it can lead to boredom with everyday life.</p> <p>Considering my own strengths and weaknesses, I noticed that I seem to be high in receptivity and embodiment, but low in embellishment and originality (and mixed when it comes to temporality). Recognizing this makes me think about paying more attention to details in my environment and playing around with more fantastical ideas, especially if I’m wanting to fuel my creativity.</p> <p>To that end, Vieten provides avenues for stretching our imagination in different ways. Some ideas for accessing different aspects of imagination deliberately include rehearsing something before doing it, brainstorming ideas, engaging all of our senses when imagining something, reframing an idea from a different perspective, and freewriting.</p> <p>Vieten also suggests creating environments conducive to being more spontaneously creative. Setting time aside to daydream, being in solitude where your mind can wander, taking walks in the woods to de-stress, or, possibly, taking psychedelic drugs (in a safe, controlled environment) can all help us disengage our DMN and allow creative thoughts to enter more freely.</p> <p>“One of the key ways to make imagination welcome is to remove the practical pressures of the world,” she writes.</p> <p>Imagine That is full of suggestions for unleashing your imagination, all based on the emerging science of imagination that Vieten and her colleagues (and others) are exploring.</p> <p>But while the book reads mostly as a self-help guide, there’s also an important message about why using our imagination is beneficial to society as a whole. Too many of us are experiencing the hopelessness and despair that come with being alive right now, writes Vieten. It’s too easy to get lost in the negative news cycles and focus on all of the problems in the world, making it more difficult to imagine anything better for our collective future.</p> <p>Learning how to engage our imagination more readily can create a sense of hope in our current situation. Not only can it bring more joy and aliveness to our individual lives, countering malaise, it can also lead to new ways of collaborating with others and innovating to solve societal problems, thereby providing a better life for everyone.</p> <p>“So many of the issues facing us locally and globally are rooted in our collective inability to imagine new solutions, alternative futures, creative pathways forward that could build a world that promotes thriving for all,” writes Vieten. “My deepest hope is that [you] take a deeper dive into the science, the practice, and the magic of imagination and [see] how it can re-enchant your life and our world.”</p> <p>Jill Suttie, Psy.D., is Greater Good’s former book review editor and now serves as a staff writer and contributing editor for the magazine. She received her doctorate of psychology from the University of San Francisco in 1998 and was a psychologist in private practice before coming to Greater Good.</p> <p>A father of three reflects on how becoming a parent taught him about love and helped him grow as a human being.</p> <p>While drug-induced mystical experiences can have benefits, research suggests they may not be enough to create lasting change.</p> <p>Despite how advanced robots have become, getting them to feel the way humans do is an incredibly complex challenge.</p> <p>What does it actually take to put people over politics? Republican and Democrat students discover ways to resist the pull to demean or villainize people with whom they strongly disagree.</p> <p>Discover how writing about our ancestors can strengthen our sense of identity, deepen gratitude, and help us find meaning in our own lives.</p> <p>The Greater Good Science Center studies the psychology, sociology, and neuroscience of well-being, and teaches skills that foster a thriving, resilient, and compassionate society.</p> <p>© 2026 The Greater Good Science Center at the University of California, Berkeley</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/article/item/how_your_imagination_can_work_for_you_or_against_you" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9675"> <h2>#9675. Pastina Soup (Italian Penicillin)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Pastina-Soup-1-scaled.jpg" alt="Pastina Soup (Italian Penicillin)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>This soup is my new go-to when my family is sick. The broth here is AMAZING – light, flavorful, and nourishing. Absolute comfort food.</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 1, 2026</p> <p>What an awesome soup recipe! The family loved it! It will be on repeat in our home especially with the kids asking for more!!! Thank you.</p> <p>Like, slurp that savory broth and go back for a third bowl kind of good.</p> <p>My daughter got sick last week, which means that our whole family got sick last week. And when I get sick, I lose two things: 1) my appetite, and 2) my interest in cooking.</p> <p>This pastina soup truly SAVED us last week. It is:</p> <p>I can’t say enough about how much I loved this last week. I sat down at the table with a steamy bowl with extra parm on top, and found myself repeatedly going back for “just one more scoop” of the broth over those tiny stars, even though I swore I hadn’t been feeling hungry just a moment earlier.</p> <p>My girls were pretty excited about eating tiny star pasta with olive oil + Parmesan, while Bjork and I ladled the luscious broth over our bowls and finally tucked into some nurturing food for the first time in several days.</p> <p>Pastina refers to the tiny star shaped pasta, which I found at Target, and the nickname Italian Penicillin refers to the healing nature of the savory broth – almost like a chicken noodle soup, but simpler. (And if I’m being honest, I prefer this to chicken noodle.)</p> <p>I hope you are healthy and well, physically and emotionally. But if you’re not, this is comfort meal that has been serving our family so well lately!</p> <p>I keep them real chunky, and I give them a quick sauté with olive oil before adding all the liquid just to get things extra fragrant.</p> <p>I use water and Better Than Bouillon broth base.</p> <p>Transfer to a bowl to cool down for a moment.</p> <p>And then add them right back to the broth pot.</p> <p>Source Notes: “Italian penicillin” is a nickname for pastina soup, or pastina (small pasta) in broth. It is playfully compared to medicine because of its healing vibe, being that it is a warm, nostalgic, nourishing comfort food. It originated with generations of Italian grandmothers and it has moved into the spotlight after becoming a popular trend on TikTok over the last few years. 🙂</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>This soup has become my go-to recipe when my family is sick. The broth is amazing – simple, light, flavorful, and nourishing! It’s absolute comfort food.</p> <p>Keywords: pastina soup, italian penicillin, soup recipe, simple soup recipe</p> <p>I love hearing from you! Leave a comment or rating below!</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>Easy on hand ingredients ended up very satisfying! I used orzo I had in the pantry. I did cook the veggies longer because I was trying to do two things at once and lost track of time. No big deal to cook a little longer. Husband is a good cook and he gave it a thumbs up. 🙂 So thanks!</p> <p>My 3 teenage sons devoured this! I made it for myself when I got sick thinking I’d be the only one to eat it, but the boys loved it. So simple yet cozy and flavorful. Thank you POY for another family favorite.</p> <p>Sautéing the chunky carrots, celery, onion, and garlic for 5 minutes, then simmering them in 10 cups of broth for 30 minutes before blending the vegetables with 1 to 2 cups of that broth, is a clear way to get a silky pot without cooking the pastina in it. I also like that the 1½ cups of stelline are cooked separately, drained, and tossed with a little olive oil so they don’t soak up the leftover broth overnight. If the carrot chunks are on the large side and still a bit firm at 30 minutes, do you usually just give them a few more minutes at a bare simmer, or have you found a slightly livelier bubble is fine as long as you don’t reduce the pot too far?</p> <p>Is nutritional information just for broth? 1/4 dry c of the stelline pasta you recommend is 200 calories per the box. How is each serving less calories than the pasta alone? Just looking to clarify. Broth is delicious! Thanks.</p> <p>I made this soup on a cold evening and blending the carrots, celery and onion into the broth gave it a much richer body than a plain clear broth, which my family noticed right away. I followed your tip to cook the pastina separately, and that kept the pasta from swelling and soaking up all the broth overnight. I used Better Than Bouillon as you suggest, and the flavor was deep without tasting overly salty, especially once I added the Parmesan at the end. I also liked the note about freezing half the broth, because I saved a batch for a busy weeknight and only had to cook fresh pastina. This comforting, simple soup is exactly the kind of recipe I reach for when someone in the house is feeling under the weather.</p> <p>First kiddo went down with a GI bug last night, so I figured it was the perfect time to try this recipe! I used homemade bone broth to make the soup and added a Parmesan rind while it simmered. It’s salty, brothy, and gently flavored. We’ll see how my sick one tolerates it, but my other two kids thought it was cozy and delicious. The star pasta is a fun texture.</p> <p>This is simple and delicious. I’ve made it twice now. This past time, I put the broth (sans vegetables) through a fine mesh strainer which helped get a nice and smooth texture.</p> <p>Also, grocery stores near me sell relatively small carrots. I used a one-pound bag of carrots and found that to be an appropriate amount.</p> <p>My son and husband woke up not feeling great this morning and I was running to Walmart anyway, so I decided to pick up the few things I needed to make a batch of this soup today!</p> <p>Sadly, they didn’t have the pastina pasta, so I used bowtie pasta. I also used chicken bone broth instead of the Bouillon. And I also cooked boneless skinless chicken thighs in with the broth and veggies for some extra protein.</p> <p>This was so simple and so delicious. I have a ton to freeze and a ton in the fridge for my boys to eat throughout the week as they work on feeling better.</p> <p>Simply amazing! So much flavor from such simple ingredients. I’m sensitive to garlic and onions so I kept them whole to add flavor to the broth and then discarded them before blending the veggies and the soup still had so much flavor!</p> <p>Is there any downside to using an immersion blender instead of taking it out and using a regular blender? Thanks!</p> <p>I’ve been rocking a cold for the last 1 to 2 weeks but with pregnancy, you don’t get to take anything helpful; finally got a chance to try this, and this hot silky broth is so so good. I gave it a verrrry generous amount of fresh cracked pepper along with the grated Parmesan.</p> <p>So glad you enjoyed it, and hope you feel better soon!</p> <p>Very good! I had to saute longer. The only thing is when I blended, I still got a crunch from the celery.</p> <p>Recently I’ve been making a version of this on repeat because I love the Progresso Chickarina soup and obsessed with the tiny star pasta but wanted a homemade version without 1000 ingredients lol!</p> <p>Of course I should have checked here first! Nine Conversation-Starting Movies to Watch With Your Romantic Partner</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://ggsc.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/assets/images/movies_not_to_watch_with_partner_2026_-_abcdef_-_0a21b39134b316e51cdc0dd96c5e6bca3c0093e9-fb_-_abcdef_-_94b15742ccdfc3b16fb1fe35872167fe8d42c35d.webp" alt="Nine Conversation-Starting Movies to Watch With Your Romantic Partner" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Become a subscribing member today. Help us continue to bring “the science of a meaningful life” to you and to millions around the globe.</p> <p>Greater Good Science Center • Magazine • In Action • In Education</p> <p>Movie date nights have long been a ritual of romance, from first dates to married couples’ standing nights out. You can probably name movies that leave you feeling warm, hopeful, excited, stimulated, and sometimes a little more in love with your partner.</p> <p>But sometimes, the movies we watch become more than that—they become conversation starters, litmus tests, or unexpected mirrors of our own relationships.</p> <p>These nine movies expose the underbelly of romantic relationships: the resentments, fantasies, secrets, compromises, and alternative lives that can coexist alongside love. Watching them runs the risk of cracking open a door that would be better kept closed, for the longevity of your relationship.</p> <p>Last month’s The Invite, starring and directed by Olivia Wilde, tops our list of nine movies you might want to watch without your partner—or at least be very sure you know what conversation you’re signing up for in the post-screening debrief. Each movie asks a question that might be safer left unanswered.</p> <p>What happens when you say the quiet part out loud?</p> <p>The Invite turns the dinner-party setup into an examination of everything couples are usually too embarrassed, jealous, or afraid to say to each other.</p> <p>Angela (Wilde) and Joe (Seth Rogen) portray a married couple whose relationship has become strained by years of resentment and disappointment. When Angela invites their upstairs neighbors, Piña (Penélope Cruz) and Hawk (Edward Norton), over for dinner, what begins as an attempt at connection becomes a much more revealing conversation about sex, attraction, love, and what people want from their partners, when they’re being honest.</p> <p>As Piña and Hawk probe the tension between Angela and Joe—also glimpsed through their apartment windows and in elevator encounters—they force the quiet parts of the other couple’s relationship into the open. The questions Angela and Joe were afraid to ask each other come to the surface, like, “Do we love each other anymore? Can we salvage this relationship? Do you want to be with someone new?”</p> <p>“Novelty is a powerful aphrodisiac. In long-term relationships especially, cultivating novelty—whether through stories or experiences—is key for sustaining passion,” says Esther Perel, sex therapist and consultant on The Invite, on her blog. “Maintaining a sense of mystery and surprise helps counteract the routine and repetition that can sometimes lead to a decline in desire over time.”</p> <p>We tend to think of monogamy as a set of universally accepted rules: Don’t sleep with someone else. Don’t cross the line. But long-term relationships are also built on unspoken knowledge about what our partner wants, what they find attractive, what they would never do, and what they might secretly wish they could do. Lifting the lid on that box may reveal that the relationship is beyond repair.</p> <p>What’s more important: Love or money? Would you risk the former for the latter? Can a couple withstand different answers to this question?</p> <p>David (Woody Harrelson) and Diana (Demi Moore) are a financially struggling, yet happily married, couple, who are offered $1 million if the wife spends one night with a wealthy stranger, played by Robert Redford. The movie takes a question that sounds like a parlor game and puts it inside a marriage: What, exactly, would you be willing to sacrifice for a life-changing amount of money?</p> <p>Diana’s decision to revisit the proposal after David’s initial hesitation—an uncomfortable pause that both she and the audience notice—begins her agreed-upon one-night stand.</p> <p>From there, suspicion and mistrust begin to take hold, gradually eroding the relationship and ultimately pushing Diana toward the wealthy stranger.</p> <p>What happens when a hypothetical becomes real? When money, desire, jealousy, and pride enter a marriage, it becomes much harder to separate what you thought you would do from what you did.</p> <p>Indecent Proposal can turn a hypothetical into an uncomfortable inventory of your partner’s values—and your own.</p> <p>Although it’s not every day a millionaire asks to sleep with a spouse, the question, and the length of the pause before answering, can reveal a lot about both sides.</p> <p>Can anyone be tempted, and can one handle the consequences of infidelity?</p> <p>Unfaithful, starring Diane Lane and Richard Gere, is a movie about a married suburban woman who meets a younger man and becomes increasingly drawn to him. There is no grand declaration that her marriage is over, no decision to go looking for an affair. There is simply attraction, followed by curiosity, a series of small choices that gradually lead down a road from which there is no return.</p> <p>Some people believe that infidelity happens only to certain kinds of couples—unhappy couples, disconnected couples, couples whose marriages were already in trouble. But some people in loving relationships can still notice other people, feel chemistry, or wonder what it would be like to be with someone else.</p> <p>In fact, that is part of what sucks you into Unfaithful: Richard Gere’s character is a quintessentially good husband—a devoted father, attentive partner, and decent man.</p> <p>“I often find that the affair is a form of self-discovery. It’s not that the individuals having the affairs want to leave their partners, but the people they have become. They are looking for another version of themselves—which is the most powerful variety of ‘other’ there is,” says Perel in an interview with Goop.</p> <p>A crush can remain a crush. A fantasy can remain a fantasy. But sometimes people begin feeding the attraction, creating opportunities to see the person again, or keeping secrets that gradually become more important than the relationship they are protecting.</p> <p>Interesting fact: Both Indecent Proposal and Unfaithful were directed by Adrian Lyne, who’s been married since 1974 to his wife Samantha.</p> <p>Can you love someone and still need to leave them?</p> <p>Marriage Story begins with a husband and wife listing the things they love about each other. It’s tender enough to feel like the opening of a great romance, but the film quickly reveals a more complicated reality. Inspired by director Noah Baumbach’s own divorce, the story explores what happens when the things we love about our partner begin to pull us in different directions.</p> <p>Charlie (Adam Driver) loves that Nicole (Scarlett Johansson) makes people feel comfortable, knows how to handle difficult family situations, plays with their son, knows when to push him and when to leave him alone. Nicole loves Charlie’s determination, his energy, his intelligence, and the way he throws himself into the things he loves.</p> <p>It is an intimate portrait of a couple who, despite everything that will follow, genuinely know and admire one another.</p> <p>The film follows Charlie and Nicole through the painful mechanics of divorce: lawyers, custody arrangements, money, competing versions of the marriage, and the realization that ending a relationship does not mean you stop having to deal with the person you are leaving.</p> <p>Nicole has spent years adapting herself to Charlie’s life and putting parts of her own ambitions aside. Charlie has built a career and a world around his creative work but has failed to recognize how much his wife has sacrificed to support it. Neither is simply the villain. Neither is simply the victim.</p> <p>That is one of the film’s most uncomfortable truths about long-term relationships: Love does not necessarily disappear before a marriage ends. Their issues aren’t due to flat-out incompatibility; they are problems of identity, compromise, resentment, and the slow accumulation of problems that were never fully addressed.</p> <p>Another question the movie asks is whether love is enough to make a marriage work.</p> <p>Gone Girl turns marital secrets into psychological warfare; this is anything but a love story.</p> <p>Based on Gillian Flynn’s novel, the film follows Nick Dunne (Ben Affleck) on the day his wife, Amy (Rosamund Pike) disappears. As the investigation unfolds, the image of their marriage begins to unravel, leaving everyone—including the audience—to wonder whether Nick killed her.</p> <p>At the heart of the film is a deeply unsettling possibility about how little access we have to another person’s reality.</p> <p>One of the qualities that relationship researchers have found important is emotional responsiveness: the feeling that your partner understands you, validates your perspective, and cares about your well-being. In other words, a healthy relationship depends less on “I know everything about you” than on “I feel safe being known by you.”</p> <p>In Eyes Wide Shut, Alice (Nicole Kidman) and Bill Harford (Tom Cruise) appear to have a comfortable marriage—secure in the routines and flow of the life they built together. That is until Alice tells her husband about a sexual fantasy involving another man.</p> <p>Bill becomes consumed by the idea of what his wife has imagined. The fantasy begins to feel like a secret life, and the distinction between imagining something and wanting it becomes increasingly difficult for him to see.</p> <p>According to Perel, our “sexual fantasies are a fount of information about our internal lives and the relational dynamics of our partnerships.”</p> <p>People also can make complicated decisions about whether to disclose fantasies to their partners. Sometimes disclosure can create intimacy. Sometimes people keep fantasies private because they fear judgment or because the fantasy itself has nothing to do with what they want in real life.</p> <p>Eyes Wide Shut makes that ordinary fact feel like a threat.</p> <p>Are we living the life we actually wanted?</p> <p>In Revolutionary Road, Frank (Leonardo DiCaprio) and April Wheeler (Kate Winslet) have built the respectable suburban life they were supposed to want, in this movie set from the late 1940s to mid 1950s. But April begins to wonder whether they have mistaken a socially approved life for the life they truly desire.</p> <p>What happens when the pendulum swings too heavily toward one person’s idea of the life they could have lived, leaving the other to defend the life they have actually built? In Revolutionary Road, April’s longing for a different future increasingly collides with Frank’s investment in the life they have created together.</p> <p>Long-term relationships inevitably require compromise. But compromise can feel very different when it is experienced as a choice rather than a sacrifice. A relationship should provide a sense of “we” without erasing the “I.” Researchers have also found that relationships can be important sources of personal growth: Partners can help one another explore new identities, pursue goals, and become more fully themselves.</p> <p>Revolutionary Road painfully takes us through the psychological unraveling of Frank and April—who seem to experience their marriage as a narrowing of possibilities rather than an expansion of them.</p> <p>Content warning: The film explores difficult themes involving self-administered abortion, death, and questions autonomy.</p> <p>Can you love someone and still hurt them?</p> <p>Closer, directed by Mike Nichols and based on Patrick Marber’s play, strips relationships down to their most uncomfortable elements like attraction, jealousy, dishonesty, and the desire to be wanted.</p> <p>The film follows four people—Dan (Jude Law), Alice (Natalie Portman), Anna (Julia Roberts), and Larry (Clive Owen)—whose relationships become increasingly entangled. What begins with a chance encounter between Dan and Anna eventually develops into a complicated web of love affairs, betrayals, and shifting loyalties. It leaves viewers asking, “Do we want to be loved, or do we want to be desired?”</p> <p>The characters repeatedly demand honesty from one another, but when they get it, the truth often hurts more than the lie. They want to know whom their partners have slept with, what they felt, whom they wanted, and whether they were ever truly enough. Yet knowing the truth doesn’t necessarily bring them closer. Sometimes, it gives jealousy something concrete to attach itself to.</p> <p>Would you still love your partner if you knew the worst thing they ever did?</p> <p>The Drama takes place in the days surrounding the wedding of Emma Harwood (Zendaya) and Charlie Thompson (Robert Pattison), a young couple whose courtship seemed out of a storybook. Over drinks one night with their best man and maid of honor, they each confess the worst thing they’d done. This revelation sparks disgust and soul-searching, as they’re forced to confront the question: “Do you still love me?”</p> <p>We all seek unconditional love from our partner. The Drama stretches this promise to the breaking point, complicated by the judgment of friends who also know the ugly truth. If you dare to watch this film with your partner, you’d be wise to think twice before sharing each other’s deep, dark secrets.</p> <p>Yasmin Garaad is a freelance journalist. Her work has also been published in National Geographic, PEOPLE Magazine, Business Insider, and more.</p> <p>Sending reels on social media may seem frivolous or distracting, but it actually functions as a form of relationship maintenance.</p> <p>New research is exploring how our brains translate other people's actions into the experience of feeling loved.</p> <p>Our contributors award our annual "Greater Goodies" to the TV shows that might help you be your best self.</p> <p>What does it actually take to put people over politics? Republican and Democrat students discover ways to resist the pull to demean or villainize people with whom they strongly disagree.</p> <p>Discover how writing about our ancestors can strengthen our sense of identity, deepen gratitude, and help us find meaning in our own lives.</p> <p>The Greater Good Science Center studies the psychology, sociology, and neuroscience of well-being, and teaches skills that foster a thriving, resilient, and compassionate society.</p> <p>© 2026 The Greater Good Science Center at the University of California, Berkeley</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/article/item/nine_conversationstarting_movies_to_watch_with_your_partner" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9671"> <h2>#9671. Warning Letters Sent to Online Pharmacies Illegally Selling Schedule II Stimulants</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2022/04/manlaptopathomess25872604_1368627.jpg" alt="Warning Letters Sent to Online Pharmacies Illegally Selling Schedule II Stimulants" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) have issued joint warning letters to 2 websites for illegally selling and distributing or dispensing schedule II stimulants, including amphetamine drug products marketed as Adderall.</p> <p>The warning letters to kubapharm.com and premiumlightsupplier.com state that the websites are selling amphetamine drug products, including Adderall, that are misbranded and in violation of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Additionally, by failing to register the online pharmacies with the DEA, despite knowingly or intentionally advertising the sale of controlled substances, these websites are also in violation of the Ryan Haight Online Pharmacy Act.</p> <p>“These letters are not only a warning to the companies that illegally sell prescription medications, but they also serve as a warning to consumers who have bought or have considered buying medications online without a legitimate prescription,” said DEA Administrator Anne Milgram. “Consumers cannot trust the safety or legitimacy of pills sold on unaccredited sites.”</p> <p>In a press release, the Agency reinforced its commitment to stopping online operators illegally selling potentially harmful drug products to consumers. “These particular types of online pharmacies also undermine our efforts to help consumers safely purchase legitimate prescription medicines over the internet,” said FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf, MD. “FDA will continue partnering with DEA in an effort to safeguard public health and protect consumers who need access to these important medicines.”</p> <p>FDA and DEA warn online pharmacies illegally selling Adderall to consumers. News release. US Food and Drug Administration. Accessed April 12, 2022. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-and-dea-warn-online-pharmacies-illegally-selling-adderall-to-consumers-301524032.html</p> <p>Psychiatry Advisor, a trusted source of medical news and feature content for healthcare providers, offers clinicians insight into the latest research to inform clinical practice and improve patient outcomes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/home/topics/adhd/warning-letters-sent-to-online-pharmacies-illegally-schedule-ii-stimulants/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9670"> <h2>#9670. Fall Freezer Meals #2</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Fall-Freezer-Meals-2-1.jpg" alt="Fall Freezer Meals #2" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>These Fall Freezer Meals have been SO helpful for us. The prep is shockingly easy!</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 14, 2026</p> <p>A few months ago, I discovered what feels like a little life hack.</p> <p>I started spending an hour each month getting a few meals prepped for the month ahead. We’re talking just assembling stuff for my favorite recipes into bags and freezing it!</p> <p>And I can’t tell you how much this system makes me feel like I have my life together! It’s the best.</p> <p>The recipes this month are absolute family favorites for fall!</p> <p>And they all have cook times for Crockpot, Instant Pot, and stovetop methods. 🙂</p> <p>Hope these help make your life easier this month like they have for us!</p> <p>Everything you need is right on them. I print the cards out and attach them to the bags so I don’t have to use my phone at all for the prep or cooking.</p> <p>For the streusel: mix 4 tablespoons melted butter, 1/3 cup brown sugar, and 3/4 cup flour into small crumbles.</p> <p>Spray a muffin tin with avocado oil. Fill tins two-thirds of the way full with batter; top with streusel.</p> <p>Store muffins in an airtight container or bag in the freezer (or fridge). To reheat from frozen, microwave 45-60 seconds.</p> <p>Remove chicken from the sauce and shred. Blend sauce until smooth. Add chicken back in. Serve in tortillas with all the taco fixings you want!</p> <p>Add 1-2 cups heavy cream and 1-2 cups chicken broth (as needed). To thicken: whisk 2 tbsp. cornstarch with 2 tbsp. cold water; add and simmer.</p> <p>Whisk 1 1/2 tbsp. cornstarch in 1 1/2 tbsp. cold water; add to bubbling pot and let simmer until slightly thickened.</p> <p>Stir in 2 cups of fresh spinach and fresh cilantro just before serving.</p> <p>Serve with rice and chili crisp. I also love this with cucumber salad (thinly sliced cucumber and red onion, tossed with vinegar, avocado oil, salt, and sugar).</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>I love this idea! Spending just an hour preparing freezer meals for the month sounds like such a practical way to make busy weekdays easier. The variety is great too, especially having options like chicken tinga tacos, wild rice soup, and chickpea curry with different cooking methods. I also appreciate the printable labels and grocery lists because they make meal prep much more organized. These recipes would be especially helpful for anyone balancing a busy schedule with home-cooked meals. Thanks for sharing!</p> <p>Very interesting post. Just thinking about the option to add to instant pot. How would that work? You put everything frozen (without any other unfrozen liquid), put the lid and select the number of minutes? So everything will thaw in the IP before it pressurized?</p> <p>Hi there, how long do these recipes stay good for in the freezer? I would like to have these as back ups. Thank you.</p> <p>Love your recipes! I love curry and the recipe for Chickpea curry looks fabulous, but, my husband is not a chickpea for protein kind of guy. Can I use chicken or shrimp instead and how much would I use?</p> <p>Can you clarify the liquid added to the chicken and wild rice soup? I’m reading 5 cups broth for cooking and then another 2.5 to finish with 2 cups cream, is that right?</p> <p>Hello! Yes, it is another 1-2 cups of broth added, as needed, with the cream. You can adjust depending on how thick you like your soup.</p> <p>Thank you so much for sharing these wonderful ideas! I love your recipes. For the Chicken Wild Rice Soup- Would a combination of Heavy Cream and Whole Milk work here like in the original blog post? What ratio do you think would be best if I did that? Thank you!</p> <p>I love both the original bechamel (butter / flour / milk) method, and the heavy cream method! 🙂 For this version, I opted for the heavy cream just because it’s easier to put onto the small cards. But the bechamel is great and it will get a bit thicker than just using cream. If you want that version, I’d just make the bechamel and add it at the end, using the same quantities as in this post: https://pinchofyum.com/crockpot-chicken-wild-rice-soup</p> <p>Hi there! Always wondering about the prep for chicken thighs, how much do you trim the fat and gristle from them? It takes me so long and I’m always wondering if it’s worth doing.</p> <p>Unless it’s a big piece of fat that you can easily cut off, you can definitely skip the trimming.</p> <p>Love the recipes I have tried! Going to try the freezer prep soup and muffins. Thanks for the recipes</p> <p>Can you use chicken breast instead of chicken thighs in the tinga tacos?</p> <p>Yep! I prefer thighs because they stay a bit juicier, but chicken breasts can absolutely work. 🙂 I would pull them out of the sauce when they’re done and really kind of -chop them into shreddy chunks rather than straight shred them – maybe it’s just me, but I find that sometimes the shredding with chicken breasts can get a bit stringy.</p> <p>Hi Lindsay, Thank you so much for all of your great recipes and ideas! I really appreciate all the hard work.</p> <p>You’re so welcome! I really have enjoyed doing these for myself these last few months, so it’s fun to share them!</p> <p>Lindsay – LOVE your recipes! Question about the freezer meals. There are a couple that you say you freeze the chicken separately but on the Chicken Wild Rice Soup it looks like you put the chicken in the same bag with everything. Can you please clarify for me? Thank you!!</p> <p>Yes! 🙂 Short answer – you can put the chicken in the bag, or add it later. Either can work. Long answer – With the first batch I did in September, I left the chicken out and added it at the time of cooking (and I wrote that into those recipe cards). I liked how it cooked, but I found it was a little bit inconvenient because I didn’t always have chicken on hand when I needed it. So for round two / the set of recipes in this post, I decided to include the chicken in the bag. All these recipes now have chicken going into the bag with everything else, and all the cook times are listed with that in mind.</p> <p>These were so easy and awesome. I prepped one of everything for my friend who just had a major surgery, and another batch for my family. I hope you keep coming out with these!</p> <p>Love that you are sharing these meals with others!</p> <p>Any replacement ideas for chipotles in adobo? Worried too spicy for the kids.</p> <p>Freezer crockpot meals are great for camping. Prep is pretty much done. Put them in the crockpot and enjoy after a day of hiking and fun. Delicious!</p> <p>I’ve been freezer cooking for years and have seen nearly all the websites on the topic.</p> <p>Yours are simply THE BEST label layout I’ve ever come across! Kudos to you!</p> <p>Thank you so much Jerri! I work on these freezer meals with Jenna on our team, and the two of us really try to make them feel as user friendly as possible! 🙂</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. My husband Bjork and I live in Minnesota. Favorite things include my camera, lake days, and dark chocolate.</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p>The eBook includes our most popular 25 recipes in a beautiful, easy to download format. Enter your email and we'll send it right over!</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://pinchofyum.com/fall-freezer-meals-2" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9669"> <h2>#9669. Sloppy Joe’s with Ranch Potatoes</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Sloppy-Joes_HighRes-014-scaled.jpg" alt="Sloppy Joe’s with Ranch Potatoes" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Easy, saucy, delicious Sloppy Joe’s! My kids’ favorite dinner. Super simple to make with just a few ingredients.</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 28, 2026</p> <p>Here’s the thing – it’s humble, it’s non-fancy, but my husband and my kids are so happy when I make this for dinner.</p> <p>I’ve been on a JOURNEY with these. I tried making Sloppy Joe’s several ways this summer, since my daughter kept asking for them. But with every batch I made, she always kindly let me know that they were still “not as good as the ones at school.”</p> <p>Lucky for me (and all of us), I know several of the wonderful people who do the food service at their school. I was able to get some school recipe intel, which is how I ended up with this very simple “recipe”:</p> <p>It’s rich, and meaty, and easy, and just so very family-friendly.</p> <p>Bjork and I like ours topped with pickled jalapenos or crispy onions, and the girls, of course, like them “plain” on a squishy white bun.</p> <p>I always always make these with what we call Ranch Potatoes, which are the truly the delight of my life. In our house, it’s not Sloppy Joe’s if there’s no pile of crispy, buttery Ranch Potatoes on the side. 🙂</p> <p>Regarding diced onion, pepper, or garlic in the Sloppy Joe filling: this recipe has none. Everyone I cook for enjoys these the same (or even more?) with an uncluttered texture and just a few hits of garlic and onion powder instead, which makes this whole thing even faster and easier.</p> <p>My youngest requested this as her birthday meal this year. Hope you like it as much as we do!</p> <p>Leave it sitting undisturbed for a few minutes so that it develops a nice golden crust.</p> <p>Garlic powder, onion powder, beef bouillon, ketchup, and BBQ sauce!</p> <p>Add some water as needed to make the mixture loosen up and turn a bit glossy. It can just hang out until you’re ready to eat.</p> <p>When you’re close to eating, pop your potatoes in the oven.</p> <p>Once they’re roasty toasty, add a knob of butter and some ranch seasoning. Toss to combine. (If you don’t have ranch seasoning, just use melted butter, fresh garlic, and dill. UNREAL.)</p> <p>Load it onto a soft bun – we love this with ranch potatoes and green beans!</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>Easy, saucy, delicious Sloppy Joe’s! My kids’ favorite dinner. We love these with Ranch Potatoes!</p> <p>White garlic sauce (for dipping, as shown in the video): Whisk 1/4 cup mayo, 1/4 cup plain Greek yogurt, 1 clove grated garlic, 1-2 tablespoons water, and salt to taste.</p> <p>Making Ahead: The meat mixture is ready to go right after you add the ketchup and BBQ sauce, but I usually like to let it simmer for 30-60 minutes to really caramelize around the edges and deepen in both flavor and color. It also works perfectly to keep it warm in the crockpot after cooking!</p> <p>Keywords: sloppy joe’s, sloppy joe sandwiches, easy dinner, kid-friendly dinner</p> <p>I love hearing from you! Leave a comment or rating below!</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>Quitar Fondo provides a Spanish-language workspace for removing backgrounds from a collection of photos and checking each result. https://www.quitarfondo.online/</p> <p>This was absolutely delicious. I need to add this to my regular rotation. Huge hit with the family!</p> <p>This was a hit with my family. The ranch potatoes are such a smart side with the sloppy joes. I will make this again soon.</p> <p>The sloppy Joes were delicious and easy! I love the idea of adding beef bullion. It definitely made it taste richer. I bought a jar of that for this recipe, along with the gorgeous brioche buns, at Costco. Be prepared to add a little more water at the end. I needed to add more to make it glossy and less sticky. This will be in our regular rotation!</p> <p>Yay – glad you loved in April! I agree about the water, I’m going to update that amount. I often need a bit more as well!</p> <p>My children all ate two helpings. This never happens. And those ranch potatoes are life changing.</p> <p>Amazing! It’s the best feeling! Thanks Lauren! 🙂 🙂</p> <p>This is a simple but delicious and nostalgic recipe. I made this last night and it was a hit.</p> <p>Do you have a favorite BBQ sauce for this recipe? I’m a vegetarian so can’t taste the recipe for my family – would love a recommendation!</p> <p>I’ve used the Trader Joe’s BBQ sauce for the last few batches and I really like it! 🙂</p> <p>Hi Linda! I have used a few kinds! Most frequent ones I’ve used are Trader Joe’s Kansas City BBQ sauce, or Famous Dave’s! 🙂</p> <p>This is such a throwback to the delicious sloppy joes of my childhood, I can already taste them! I’m a vegetarian now- any suggestion of what could be used in place of the meat? Wondering if a combo of beans and mushrooms might work…. off to do some research…. 🙂</p> <p>Hi Gigi: we are also mostly vegetarian (no red meat) so I make tofu crumbles. You can find a recipe on the internet. I freeze my tofu, thaw and drain it and then shred it on the large holes of a grater. Mix with seasonings and bake in the oven. I make a big batch and then seperate them into portions and freeze. Use them for this and anything else calling for ground beef. Hope this helps.</p> <p>Thanks for this! how would you adjust this if you wanted to create this and prep ahead of time, and serve later the next day in a crockpot?</p> <p>Jumping in to add that I also frequently 1.5x or 2x this and freeze whatever we don’t eat, since it works so well as a make-ahead! Especially when I know I’m going to be hosting or serving a crowd. Then I just reheat with a bit more water and sauce or warm in the crockpot.</p> <p>Make as is, then just put on low in a crockpot to rewarm!</p> <p>Ahhhhh Sloppy Joe’s!! My kids are now in their mid-20’s and these are STILL a family favorite haha. I love making them a nostalgic meal when they’re home. Can’t wait to try your version with the beef bouillon base…sounds like a perfect addition!</p> <p>It’s so funny, I make all of this (what I think is) interesting, fun, delicious food, but then I make just regular ol Sloppy Joe’s and my family is just swooning. 🙂 Hope my kids still want me to make these for them when they’re 20!</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. My husband Bjork and I live in Minnesota. Favorite things include my camera, lake days, and dark chocolate.</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p>The eBook includes our most popular 25 recipes in a beautiful, easy to download format.
